questions.stem: You are working in a covid ward. After doffing, where will you dispose of the plastic coverall?
questions.explanation: The plastic coverall used by a healthcare worker during the COVID-19 pandemic should be disposed of in the red bin.

questions.stem: An intern asks for your advice regarding the disposal of needles from the needle tip cutter after a vaccine drive. Which of the following bins will you advise her to discard them in?
questions.explanation: Waste sharps including metals (both used, discarded, and contaminated metal sharps) are to be discarded in the white bin.

questions.stem: Chemical waste is disposed in bags.
questions.explanation: Chemical waste is disposed of in yellow-colored containers or non-chlorinated plastic bags.

questions.stem: Which of the following is false regarding a disaster?
options: Occurrence that causes damage to life and property
Occurrence that has the potential to cause disruption or damage to people
Occurrence that causes deterioration of health and health services
Occurrence that can cause substantial economic harm
questions.explanation:
A disaster is defined as any occurrence that causes damage, ecological disruption, loss of human life, or deterioration of health and health services. It usually requires an extraordinary response from outside the affected community or area.
A hazard is any phenomenon that has the potential to cause disruption or damage to people and their environment.

questions.stem: Which type of natural disaster causes the most deaths?
questions.explanation:
Hydrological natural disasters cause the most deaths.
The Disaster Information Management System of Deslnventar classifies natural disasters into five major categories. They are:
Geophysical - earthquakes, tsunamis, and volcano eruptions
Hydrological - floods, debris flow, and landslides
Meteorological - cyclones, tornadoes, extreme temperatures, sandstorms, blizzards etc.
Climatological - drought, forest wildfire, glacial lake outburst etc.
Biological - epidemics and insect infestations

questions.stem: Which of the following steps of disaster management is in correct order?
questions.explanation:
The correct order is Disaster impact – Response – Rehabilitation – Mitigation. Disaster management includes three aspects:
Disaster impact and response: It involves immediate management of mass casualties as follows:
Search, rescue, and first-aid
Field care
Triage
Tagging
Identification of dead
Rehabilitation or recovery: It involves the restoration of the pre-disaster conditions by taking steps such as:
Water supply
Basic sanitation and personal hygiene
Food safety
Vector control
Mitigation: Measures designed either to prevent hazards from causing disaster or to reduce the effects of the disaster. This also includes preparedness for any impending disasters or in
disaster-prone areas.
[[IMG:1]]

questions.stem: Which of the following is false about disaster management?
options: Measures to prevent hazards are designed in mitigation phase
Rescue and evacuation occur in recovery phase
Measures on vector control are done in rehabilitation phase
Field care and tagging are done in disaster impact and response phase
questions.explanation:
Rescue and evacuation occur in the response phase, not in the recovery phase. Disaster management includes three aspects:
Disaster impact and response: It involves immediate management of mass casualties as follows:
Search, rescue, and first-aid
Field care
Triage
Tagging
Identification of dead
Rehabilitation or recovery: It involves the restoration of the pre-disaster conditions by taking steps such as:
Water supply
Basic sanitation and personal hygiene
Food safety
Vector control
Mitigation: Measures designed either to prevent hazards from causing disaster or to reduce the effects of the disaster. This also includes preparedness for any impending disasters or
disaster-prone areas.
[[IMG:1]]

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most common disease after a disaster?
questions.explanation:
Gastroenteritis is the most commonly reported disease after a disaster.
It occurs due to contamination of water supply, damage to the sewerage system, overcrowding and poor sanitation. Therefore, supply of safe drinking water and proper disposal of excreta are the most practical and effective strategies of disease prevention in the post–disaster period.

questions.stem: Which of the following diseases is not commonly seen in the post-disaster period?
questions.explanation:
Leishmaniasis is not commonly seen in the post-disaster period. Diseases that are commonly seen in the post-disaster phase are:
Gastroenteritis (most common)
Acute respiratory infections
Leptospirosis
Rickettsiosis
Rabies
Equine encephalitis

questions.stem: A district in Andhra Pradesh reported severe drought. Which of the following vitamin deficiencies would you expect to see in this population?
questions.explanation: Vitamin A deficiency is the most common deficiency in areas of famines and droughts. It leads to xerophthalmia and blindness.

questions.stem: Following a drought in Bihar, the government launched an immediate mass vaccination program. Which of the following vaccines is recommended in such cases?
questions.explanation:
Measles vaccination is recommended for infants and children, immediately following a disaster. This should be given along with vitamin A supplementation as measles can exacerbate vitamin A deficiency.
The vaccination of infants and children against measles is one of the most important public health response measures during a humanitarian crisis when less than 90% of the children or an unknown percentage have already been vaccinated against measles.
Measles and polio vaccines are recommended immediately after an emergency. Option A: Cholera vaccine is not recommended.
Option B: Hepatitis A vaccine is recommended at the outset of an outbreak.
Option C: Tetanus vaccine is recommended in the early stages and post-emergency stage.

questions.stem: Immediately following a disaster, mass vaccination of which of the following vaccines does the WHO recommend?
questions.explanation: The WHO does not recommend typhoid, cholera, and rabies vaccines for mass vaccination after a disaster. However, high-risk populations are recommended to take the cholera vaccine. The rabies vaccine is given only for post-exposure prophylaxis.

questions.stem: You are a field doctor at the site of an earthquake. You assist in rapidly classifying the injured on the basis of the likelihood of their survival and need for intervention. What is this process called?
questions.explanation:
The process of rapidly classifying the injured in a disaster on the basis of severity of injury and likelihood of survival with prompt medical intervention is called triage. It is carried out at the site of disaster.
Tagging is the identification of patients in a disaster with tags stating their name, age, place of origin, triage category, diagnosis, and initial treatment.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about triage?
questions.explanation:
In triage, green signifies low priority or ambulatory patients and those with minor illnesses.
An internationally accepted four-color coded system, with red having the highest priority is used commonly here.

questions.stem: Which of the following is correct about reverse triage?
options: Classifying the victims based on the severity of their injuries and their survival with treatment
Highest preference is given to severely injured patients
More injured victims are given the lowest preference
Color coding is done with red as the highest priority.
questions.explanation:
Reverse triage is a situation where the less injured are treated earlier than the ones that are injured more.
This is used in wars and military settings, where soldiers may need to return to the field of battle soon after treatment. It is also done when there is a scarcity of medical resources after a disaster.

questions.stem: What is the level of residual chlorine to be maintained in the water bodies after a disaster?

However, during a disaster, there is an increased risk of fecal contamination of water sources from the sewage systems. Therefore, it is necessary to increase FRC to 0.7 - 0.9 mg/L.

questions.stem: Barosinusitis is likely to be seen in which of the following patients?
options: A person who is suffering from mountain sickness
A patient Infected by gas-forming bacteria
A patient diagnosed with Aspergillus sinusitis
A diver who developed decompression sickness
questions.explanation:
Barosinusitis occurs in decompression sickness or Caisson's disease. It is due to the sudden expansion of air in the sinuses.
It can be seen in:
Divers who ascend rapidly from deep-sea (high pressure) to the surface of the earth (low pressure)
Pilots of unpressurized aircraft or mountaineers who rapidly ascended from the surface of the earth (high-pressure zone) to a high altitude (low-pressure zone)
Under high pressure, gases get compressed, and their solubility increases. When a person is in deep-sea (high-pressure zone) for a long time, an increased amount of nitrogen gets dissolved in his body. When he suddenly comes back to the surface (atmospheric pressure or a low-pressure zone), the solubility of gases decreases and they escape from the dissolved state forming nitrogen bubbles.
These bubbles can cause sudden expansion of air in various parts of the body such as the middle ear (barotitis), sinuses (barosinusitis), beneath teeth (barodontalgia), intestinal loops (abdominal distension), and emphysema.
Nitrogen bubbles can also cause chokes (dyspnoea), bends (joint pain), and prickles (nerve irritation).
The definitive treatment for Caisson's disease is recompression.

questions.stem: Workers working at which of the following industries require periodical examination on a daily basis?

questions.stem: Serial chest X-rays of an elderly man reveal progressive massive fibrosis. Which of the following pneumoconiosis is associated with this?
questions.explanation:
Progressive massive fibrosis (PMF) is associated with anthracosis. PMF classically develops in anthracosis and silicosis.
Exposure to coal dust causes progressive lung injury called anthracosis. Initially, it manifests as simple coal worker pneumoconiosis, which occurs after exposure for 10–12 years and is reversible. Later, it can progress to progressive massive fibrosis (PMF) which is irreversible.

questions.stem: Bronchoalveolar lavage from a patient with pneumoconiosis showed Micropolyspora faeni. What is the diagnosis?

Farmer's lung is a hypersensitivity pneumonitis caused by thermophilic actinomycetes
like Saccharopolyspora rectivirgula (formerly known as Micropolyspora faeni). It occurs due to inhalation of moldy hay and grains causing an immunological reaction.
Woodworker's lung is a hypersensitivity pneumonitis caused by Alternaria species, and Bacillus subtilis in persons exposed to oak, cedar, pine, and mahogany dust.
Bird fancier's lung is caused by proteins derived from birds like pigeons and parakeets in persons exposed to their feathers and droppings.
Malt worker's lung is caused by Aspergillus species in persons exposed to barley.

Protection

Periodic inspection

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true about occupational cancer?
options: Age of incidence is same as compared to general population for the same cancer
The localization of the tumor is variable within a particular industry
The most common occupational cancer is squamous cell carcinoma
Onset of cancer does not occur after the person has left the industry
questions.explanation:
The most common occupational cancer is squamous cell carcinoma of the skin. It is associated with exposure to radiation, dyes, and coal tar.
In occupational cancers, the age of incidence of cancer is earlier than that in the general population, affected by the same cancer type. The onset of cancer can occur even after leaving the industry. The localization of the cancer is remarkably constant for a particular industry.

questions.stem: Cystoscopy performed on a patient with painless hematuria showed a fungating mass in the bladder. Exposure to all of the following agents can cause this disease except:
questions.explanation:

questions.stem: A young woman is being evaluated for infertility. She gives a history of being employed in the printing industry. Exposure to which of the following is likely to cause this situation?
questions.explanation:
A woman working in the printing industry is likely to suffer from infertility due to lead toxicity.
More industrial workers are exposed to lead than to any other toxic metal. Occupational exposure to lead is seen in several industries including the manufacturing of storage batteries, glass, shipbuilding, printing, potteries, and rubber industries.
The effects of lead poisoning include abdominal colic, blue-line on the gums (Burton's line), stippling of red cells, anemia, wrist & foot drop, headache, and convulsions. In young or pregnant women, prolonged lead exposure can cause miscarriage, stillbirth, premature birth, and low birth weight.

Masks protect the mouth/nose and respirators protect the respiratory tract from airborne infectious agents.
Goggles – protect eyes.
Face shields – protect face, mouth, nose, and eyes.

questions.stem: What is the correct order for the process of communication?
questions.explanation:
The correct order for the process of communication is: SenderMessageChannelReceiverFeedback
The sender (communicator) is the originator of the message. A message is the information which the communicator transmits to his audience. Channel is the media of communication between the sender and the receiver (e.g., interpersonal communication, mass media, traditional or folk media). The audience who receives, understands, and acts upon the message is called the receiver. Feedback is the reaction to the message which flows from the receiver to the sender.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not an approach to health education?
questions.explanation:
Socio-environmental approach is not an approach to health education. There are four approaches to health education:
Regulatory approach- external control or laws placed on people by the government. Ex: Child Marriage Act, No smoking in public places, Helmet law
Service approach- government aims at providing health services to the people at their doorsteps. Its drawback is that people will not accept a service, even if it is offered free of cost unless it is based on their felt needs. Ex: Government provided latrines free of cost yet people did not use them because its need was not felt
Health education approach- creates awareness of health needs and problems. Awareness leads to motivation which includes the stages of interest, evaluation, and decision-making. It is followed by acceptance of the new idea which becomes part of his existing values, known as internalization. Ex: Adoption of ORS for diarrhea
Primary health care approach- delivery of health services with the active involvement of people. Principles of community participation and intersectoral coordination are stressed here. Its objective is to help individuals become self-reliant in health matters. Ex: People receive guidance from healthcare providers (Rogi Kalyana Samiti, Mahila Arogya Samiti).

questions.stem: In which model of health education does internalization occur?

Medical model: transfer of proven medical information into education. It does not bridge the gap between knowledge and behavior.
Motivation model: creates awareness of health needs and problems. Awareness leads
to motivation which includes stages of interest, evaluation, and decision-making. It is followed by acceptance of the new idea which becomes part of his existing values, known as internalization.
Social intervention model: focuses on changing the social environment which subsequently shapes the behavior of individual and the community.

questions.explanation:
The best method to teach an urban slum about ORS is by demonstrations.
Demonstration is a carefully prepared presentation on how to perform a certain task or skill or procedure. It shows the step-by-step process of a task. It arouses interest and incites ‘learning by doing,’ and ‘seeing is believing’ philosophies.

questions.stem: Which of the following is used to obtain consensus forecasts among a large number of people?
questions.explanation:
Delphi method is a systematic interactive forecasting method, which is used to obtain a consensus forecast among a large number of people. It determines the degree of agreement on a topic.
This can help in setting priorities or selecting alternatives in planning. This method uses questionnaires, which are answered by experts in two or more rounds.

questions.stem: What is total communication used for?
questions.explanation:
The philosophy of total communication is used in the education of hearing-impaired children.
It requires the incorporation of aural, oral, and manual modes of communication for effective communication with and among hearing-impaired people.

questions.stem: In which of the given scenarios would you use the GATHER approach?
questions.explanation:
The GATHER approach is mainly used for counseling, like in contraceptive counseling, wherein a person is helped to make a decision about health.
GATHER stands for:
G – Greet
A – Ask
T – Tell options or give answers
H – Help in making choices
E – Explain everything about the decision
R – Return for follow-up

questions.stem: SPIKES protocol is for:
questions.explanation:
SPIKES protocol is for breaking bad news.
Each letter represents a phase in the six-step sequence.
S - setting
P - perception
I - invitation or information
K - knowledge
E - empathy
S - summarizing or strategizing
Key components of the SPIKES strategy include:
Demonstrating empathy
Acknowledging and validating the patient's feelings
Exploring the patient's understanding and acceptance of the bad news
Providing information about possible interventions

questions.stem: Which of the following is the ultimate long-term desired state towards which all the resources are directed?
questions.explanation:
The goal is the ultimate desired state towards which objectives and resources are directed. It is long-term and not constrained by time or resources.
The plan is the blueprint for taking action in order to achieve the goal.
Option A: Target refers to the quantifiable and achievable mid-term endpoints in the plan. Option B: Mission describes the cause of the existence of the programme.
Option D: The objectives are short-term endpoints. They are precise points in the plan. They are either achieved or unachieved.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a set of rules that helps ensure maximum use of the resources and efforts?
questions.explanation:
Procedure is a set of rules for carrying out work. It helps to ensure the maximum use of resources and efforts.
Option B: Programme is a sequence of activities designed to implement policies and accomplish objectives.
Option C: Schedule is a time sequence for the work to be done.
Option D: Target refers to the quantifiable and achievable mid-term endpoints in the plan.

questions.stem: A team of doctors is planning to conduct a survey on the prevalence of infective diarrhea in a village. What is the correct sequence of steps involved in the planning of this activity?
questions.explanation:
The planning cycle includes the following steps:
Analysis of the health situation
Establishment of objectives and goals
Assessment of resources
Fixing priorities
Writing-up of a formulated plan
Programming and implementation
Monitoring
Evaluation

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a component of the evaluation of health programs?
questions.explanation:

Relevance
Adequacy
Accessibility
Acceptability
Effectiveness
Efficiency
Effect or impact

Establish standards and criteria
Plan the methodology to be applied
Gather information
Analyze the results
Take action
Re-evaluate

questions.stem: Which committee had recommended a bachelor degree in medical education for rural health services?
options: High-level expert group on universal health coverage
Committee on Integration of Health Services
questions.explanation:
The high-level expert group (HLEG) on universal health coverage under the aegis of the Planning Commission of India suggested a 3.5 year bachelor degree course in medical education for rural health services.
This was planned for the 12th five-year plan (2012-2017). The degree given was B.Sc Community Health, and these rural health care practitioners were to be called community health officers.

questions.stem: Who was appointed as the chairman of the Health Survey and Development Committee in 1943?
questions.explanation:
Sir Joseph William Bhore was appointed as the chairman of the Health Survey and Development Committee in 1943. This committee was hence named the Bhore committee.

questions.stem: Which health planning committee proposed the 3 million plan?
questions.explanation:
The 3 million plan was proposed by the Bhore Committee. It proposed to set up the following in the long-term:
Primary health units with 75-bedded hospitals for each 10,000 to 20,000 population
Secondary units with 650 beds
District hospitals with 2,500 beds
As a short-term measure, it was proposed that each PHC must cater to 40,000 people and have:
2 medical officers, 4 public health nurses, 1 nurse
4 midwives, 4 dais, 2 sanitary inspectors, 2 health assistants
1 pharmacist
15 other class IV employees

questions.stem: What is the provision of preventive, curative, and promotional health services to every individual called?
questions.explanation: Comprehensive health care as stated by the Bhore committee means giving integrated preventive, curative, and promotional health care to every individual, irrespective of their ability to pay.

questions.stem: In the inventory management of drug stores, which of the following is a component of the VED method?
questions.explanation:
The 'D' in the VED method stands for desirable.
VED is a method of inventory management used mainly in drug stores and pharmacies.
The drugs are classified in three categories as follows:
V - Vital drugs. Items whose absence cannot be tolerated (10% of total items).
E - Essential drugs. Items whose absence can be tolerated for some time (40% of total items).
D - Desirable drugs. Items whose absence can be tolerated for a long time (50% of total items).

questions.stem: Which article of the Indian Constitution confers Right to Life to the citizens of India?
questions.explanation:
The Right to Life is given in Article 21 of the Indian Constitution.
Option A: Article 11 defines the right of the parliament to regulate the right of citizenship by law. Option C: Article 23 defines the prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labor.
Option D: Article 25 defines the freedom of conscience and free profession, practice, and propagation of religion.

questions.stem: Which of the following is part of the concurrent list of the Indian Constitution?
options: Fishing and fisheries beyond territorial waters
questions.explanation:
Adulteration of food is included under the concurrent list.
The legislative section of the seventh schedule is divided into three lists:
Union list - a list of 100 items on which the parliament has exclusive power to legislate
State list - a list of 61 items on which the state government has exclusive power to legislate

questions.stem: Which of the following is not included in the secondary level of the healthcare system?
questions.explanation: Medical colleges are included in the tertiary level of the health care system, which is also the second referral centre.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not an element of primary healthcare?
questions.explanation:
Providing physical rehabilitation is not an element of primary health care. Primary health centers
(PHCs) are only responsible for the popularization and mainstreaming of PMR in the community.
Primary health care refers to essential health care made universally available to individuals and acceptable to them, through their full participation and at a cost the community and country can afford.

questions.stem: All of the following are pillars of primary health care except:
questions.explanation: Health education is an element of primary health care, not a pillar.

questions.stem: Which of the following statement is false regarding ASHA workers?
options: Few of their responsibilities are integrated with Anganwadi workers
They should have formal education at least up to class 10
A population of 1000 should have at least 1 ASHA
They have to procure ORS, OCPs, IFA tablets from CHC
questions.explanation:
Accredited social health activist (ASHA) workers do not need to procure supplies from CHCs. They only act as depot holders for certain essential supplies so that they are readily available to their community.
These essential supplies may include ORS, contraceptives, iron-folic acid tablets, chloroquine, disposable delivery kits, oral contraceptive pills, condoms, etc.

questions.stem: Which of the following is incorrect regarding Anganwadi workers?
options: One AWW serves a population of 5000
They are appointed under the ICDS scheme
They link the community with the health services
Their responsibilities include counsel for immunization, health education, and nutrition
questions.explanation:
The norm is one Anganwadi worker (AWW) per 400-800 population.
Anganwadi workers (AWW) are allotted under the integrated child development services (ICDS). AWW are selected from the community they are to serve and act as links between the community and health services. They are mostly part-time workers.
Responsibilities of an AWW include:
Health checkups and growth chart maintenance
Counsel women on birth preparedness, importance of safe delivery, immunization and contraception and prevention of common infections including STD and RTIs.
Nutrition
Health education
Non-formal school education
Referral services

questions.stem: One male health assistant is posted for a population of:
questions.explanation: One male and female health assistant are required for a population of 30,000 in plain areas and of 20,000 in hilly or remote areas.

questions.stem: How many people does a Mahila Arogya Samiti member cater to?
questions.explanation: 1 Mahila Arogya Samiti member is appointed for a population of 250-500 (covering about 50-100 households).

questions.stem: Which of the following duties would be performed by a male health worker?
questions.explanation:
The duties of a male health worker include chlorination of water bodies, distribution of conventional contraceptives, and reproductive and child health services.
Maintanence of eligible couple registers (part of family planning activities) and immunization are duties of female health workers.
Health workers (male and female) are 1 per 5000 in plains and 1 per 3000 in remote or hilly areas.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a duty of a female health worker?
questions.explanation:
Malaria surveillance activities, in accordance with the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme, are the duty of a male health worker.
Health workers (male and female) are 1 per 5000 in plains and 1 per 3000 in remote or hilly areas.

questions.stem: Which of the following are not involved in providing antenatal support to pregnant women?
questions.explanation:

Health workers (male and female) - 1 per 5000 in plains and 1 per 3000 in hilly or remote areas.
Health assistants (male and female) - 1 per 30,000 in plains and 1 per 20, 000 in remote or hilly areas.
Anganwadi workers - 1 per 400-800 in plains and 1 per 300-800 in hilly or remote areas.

questions.stem: How many people does one sub-center in a hilly or remote area cater to?
questions.explanation:

Maternal and child health, family planning
Counseling for abortion and adolescent health care
Water quality monitoring and sanitation promotion
Assistance to school health services
Field visits and treating minor ailments
Training of ASHA and birth attendants
Disease surveillance and National Health Programme functions

questions.stem: What should be the maximum number of female health workers at a sub-center?
questions.explanation:
Two female health workers are to be at a sub-center as proposed by the Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS).
There are two types of sub-centers:
Type A - It has all facilities except for conducting deliveries. It can be upgraded to Type B.

questions.explanation:

questions.explanation: An urban CHC caters to a population of 5 lakh in a metropolitan city and 2.5 lakh in other cities. An urban PHC caters to a population of 50,000.

questions.stem: Which of the following is incorrect regarding the staffing at urban primary health centers?
questions.explanation:

questions.stem: Which of the following is the principal unit of administration in India?
questions.explanation:
The principal unit of administration in India is the district under a collector.
Under districts are the sub-divisions, tahsils or talukas, municipalities or corporations, villages, panchayats, etc. As of 2021, there are 748 districts in India.

questions.stem: Which of the following is incorrectly matched?
questions.explanation:
The Panchayat Samiti or Janpada Panchayat operates at the block level.
Panchayati Raj is a three-tier structure of rural self-government in India. It operates at the following levels:
Panchayat at the village level (includes Gram Sabha, Gram Panchayat, and Nyaya Panchayat)
Panchayat Samiti or Janpada Panchayat at the block level
Zilla Parishad at the district level

questions.stem: Community or village health guides are selected by:
questions.explanation:
Village health guides (VHGs) are selected by the medical officer-in-charge (MO).
2-3 candidates are put forward by the community for the position of a VHG. The MO selects one of them after consultation with the block development officer and field staff.

questions.stem: As a PHC medical officer, you would keep all of the following in mind while selecting a village health guide except:
options: They must be above 45 years of age
They must be a resident of the community that they will serve
They must be educated up to 6th grade
They should be able to spare 2-3 hours in a day for community work
questions.explanation:
Village health guides (VHG) are chosen by the medical officer-in-charge (including PHC MO). Age is not a criterion for selection.
The VHG scheme was introduced in 1977. Guidelines for choosing a VHG include:
They can be of either sex but must be residents of the village
They must know to read and write and have education up to 6th grade
They must be able to spare around 2-3 hours a day for community work
They must be acceptable to all parts of the community
VHGs are trained for 2-3 months before beginning work. The norm is to have 1 VHG per 1000 population.

questions.stem: Which of the following public health centers do First Referral Units (FRUs) and non-FRUs belong to?
questions.explanation:
First Referral Units (FRUs) and non-FRUs belong to the Community Health Centers (CHCs).
The Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS) guidelines are a code of standards for uniformity in health facilities in the Indian public health system, under the National Health Mission (NHM), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW), India. It aims to provide guidance on the infrastructure, human resources, drugs, diagnostics, equipment, quality, and governance requirements for delivering health services at all levels of facilities in the system.
The 2022 edition of IPHS mainly concentrates on comprehensive primary health care, increasing the human workforce, decentralized access to healthcare, and better implementation of universal health coverage.

questions.stem: A district has a population of 20 lakhs. According to the IPHS 2022 guidelines, approximately how many beds should the district public health system have for this population?
questions.explanation:
In a district having a population of 20 lakhs, the number of beds the district public health system should have is given as follows: 2000 essential and 4000 desirable.
According to IPHS 2022 norms for the number of beds in district hospitals, 1 bed pe	r 1000 population is essential and 2 beds per thousand population would be desirable.
Therefore, in a population of 20,00,000 the district public health system should have 2000 essential and 4000 desirable beds.
The essential number of beds should be achieved through the public health system of tertiary care (medical colleges), secondary care (DH, SDH, CHCs), and primary care in the district (PHCs and CHCs).

questions.stem: Which of the following is not true about district and sub-district hospitals?
options: All districts need at least two district hospitals.
The minimum essential number of beds in a sub-district hospital is 100.
All districts do not need a sub-district hospital.
DNB training can be done in district hospitals.
questions.explanation:
Every district should have at least one comprehensively functioning district hospital (DH).
District hospitals and subdistrict hospitals provide secondary care health services. Every district should have at least one comprehensively functioning DH. Districts with a population of less than 5 lakhs and with a functional DH do not need a subdistrict hospital (SDH). Districts with a population of 5–10 lakhs can have one SDH. For a population of more than 10 lakhs, 1 SDH is needed for every 10 lakh population.
The three pillars of district hospital services are providing clinical care, providing a knowledge hub for capacity development, and public health programs.
Important functions of DHs:
Providing curative services
Palliative and rehabilitative services
Implementation of health programs
Drugs and diagnostic services
Administrative and other support services
Health promotion and prevention, education

questions.stem: You are conducting a study to determine the mean height of children visiting the local PHC. Which type of statistical study is being done here?
questions.explanation:
A study to determine the mean height of children is an example of a descriptive statistical study.
Descriptive statistics are the statistical methods that merely organize, describe or summarize the actual data available. For example, a study determining the mean blood pressure of patients visiting a PHC on a single day.
Analytical statistics are the second major category of epidemiological studies, after descriptive statistics. The objective of an analytical study is to test the hypothesis.
An observational study is an empiric investigation in which the objective is to establish a relationship between cause and effect. It falls under the category of analytical statistics.
It is performed when controlled experimentation cannot be feasibly used to determine a hypothesis. For example, in the case of cigarette smoking causing lung cancer, it would be unethical and not feasible to conduct a controlled experiment. So, an observational study is preferred.
Inferential statistics involve inductive reasoning i.e., generalizing observations to a population after having observed only a sample. An example of such a study would be a study determining the expected success rate of vasectomy
Theoretical statistics is a mathematical approach to describe something, predict events, or analyze the relationship between things. Some of the concepts of theoretical statistics are mean, median, mode, standard deviation and correlation.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about statistical terms is incorrect?
options: Population is the universe about which an investigator wishes to draw conclusions
A sample is a representative subset of the population that is being studied
An element is a group of observations in the population
A population need not be only people but can be measurements too
questions.explanation:
An element is a single observation in a study. For example, in a study of blood pressure values, the blood pressure value of one person is an element.
In a statistical study, the population refers to the group about which information is to be gathered. The composition of the population in terms of its age, sex, occupation, cultural characters, etc need to be defined before a study is conducted. The population need not consist of just people but can also be made of measurements. For example, in a study of blood glucose measurements in Indians, the population consists of the blood glucose measurements.
The part/subset of the population, which is being studied is known as a sample. For example, in a questionnaire-based study on cervical cancer in a population, the sample would include females attending the out-patient departments of a hospital. This is a subset of the entire population.
[[IMG:1]]

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about probability is true? (Probability of event occurring is p)
questions.explanation:
If the probability of an event occurring is 1, it means there is an absolute certainty that the event will occur.
The addition rule and multiplication rule can be used to calculate the probability of an event. The addition rule is used to calculate the combined probability of the occurrence of two or more mutually exclusive events. The multiplication rule is used to calculate the combined probability of two or more statistically independent events occurring together.
Probability values range from 0 (no probability) to 1 (absolute certainty). So negative value of p is not possible.
Since p is the probability of an event occurring and q is the probability of the event not occurring, q = 1 - p

questions.stem: In which of the following processes is binomial distribution widely used?
questions.explanation:
Binomial distribution is widely used in genetic counseling.
Binomial distribution helps determine the probability of occurance of a specific combination of mutually exclusive independent events. In a binomial distribution, there are only two possible events like Yes/No or Male/Female or Alive/Dead. The results of the distribution gives the probabilities of obtaining an exact number of successes in a series of independent trials.
For example, the inheritence of cystic fibrosis follows a binomial distribution. There are:
Two possible events - inheriting the disease/ not inheriting it
Events are mutually exclusive - one person cannot both have the disease and not have it
Independent possibilities - if one child has inherited it, this will not affect if the other child will inherit it.
The physician using this technique can explain to the patients the probabilities of their children suffering from the disease.

questions.stem: If the events A and B are mutually exclusive events, what is the probability of either A or B occurring?
questions.explanation:
If the events A and B are mutually exclusive, then the probability of either A or B occuring is given by,
p (A or B) = p (A) + p (B)
This is as per the addition rule of probability.
The probability of both the mutually exclusive events happening at the same time is given by, p (A and B) = p (A) x p (B)
The probability of any of two mutually non-exclusive events occuring at a point of time is given by, p (A or B) = p (A) + p (B) - p (A and B)
If p(A) and p(B) are the only two outcomes possible in a given event then, p (A) + p (B) = 1
For example, probability of patient suffering from lung cancer dying within 5 years and probability of patient suffering from lung cancer surviving these 5 years adds upto 1.

questions.stem: You are conducting a study on birth weight. As per your data, the probability of a baby having birth weight <2500 grams is 0.50 and of having birth weight of 2500-2ŠŠŠ grams is 0.20. What is the probability that a baby will have a birth weight of < 3kg?
questions.explanation:
The probability that a baby will have a birth weight of < 3kg is 0.70.
In this scenario, the probability of having a baby with BW < 2500 grams, p (A) = 0.50 and that of having a baby with BW between 2500 – 2ŠŠŠ grams, p (B) = 0.20.
Since both events are mutually exclusive, i.e., they cannot happen together, it satisfies the condition for the addition rule of probability.
Thus, the probability of having a baby that weighs less than 3 kilos is, p (A or B) = p (A) + p (B) = 0.50 + 0.20 = 0.70.
If p(A) and p(B) were non-mutually exclusive events, then the probability would have been calculated by
p(A or B) = p(A) + p(B) - p(A and B).

questions.stem: You select 3 people from a population where the prevalence of anemia is 20% .What is the probability that all the three randomly selected people from the population would have anemia?
questions.explanation:
In the given scenario, the probability of all 3 randomly selected individuals having anemia is 0.008.
In this scenario, the prevalence of anemia is 20%.
So, the probability of a person having anemia in the given population (p) = 20/100 = 0.2.
If selecting 3 people from the population randomly, the chance of the first person having anemia is independent of the second or third person also having it and vice versa. This satisfies the condition for the multiplication rule of probability which states that the probability of two or more statistically independent events all occurring together is equal to the product of their individual probabilities.
Thus, here the probability that all the 3 randomly selected people from the population would have anemia = 0.2 x 0.2 x 0.2 = 0.008.

questions.stem: There are 50 patients admitted in a ward of your medical college. Here 20 are girls and 30 are boys. Out of this, 10 girls and 20 boys require surgery. What is the probability that a randomly selected boy and girl both require surgery?
questions.explanation:
In the given scenario, the probability that a randomly selected boy and girl both require surgery is 1/3.
First, we have to calculate the probability of picking the boys requiring surgery and the girls requiring surgery separately. These are mutually exclusive events.
In this scenario, the probability of correctly picking a girl requiring surgery is p(A)=10/20= 1/2 The probability of correctly picking a boy requiring surgery is p(B)=20/30= 2/3
Next, we apply the multiplication rule of probability.
The probability of picking boys and girls that require surgery, p(A and B)= p(A) x p(B)= ½ x ■ = 2/ç= 1/3.

questions.stem: The chance of passing a genetic disease X by affected parents to their first child is 0.1ç. If they plan to have two children, what is the probability that both the children will have the disease?
questions.explanation:
The probability of both children having the disease is 0.025ç.
In this scenario, the chance of each child having the disease is 0.1ç. The second child having the disease is independent of the first child having it. So, the events are statistically independent.
Applying the multiplication rule of probability, the probability of both children having the disease is,
0.1ç x 0.1ç = 0.025ç.
These are non-mutually exclusive events as the first child having the trait does not rule out the chance of the second child having it.
On the other hand, the probability of one of the two children having the disease is given by, p(A or B)= p(A) + p(B) - p(A and B)= 0.1ç + 0.1ç -(0.1ç x 0.1ç)= 0.32- 0.025ç= 0.2Š44

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a measurement scale for data?
questions.explanation:
A proportion is not a measurement scale for data. It is a ratio, where the numerator is always a part of the denominator. It indicates a value as a part of the whole. It is usually expressed as a percentage.
The four scales of measurement used for data can be remembered with the mnemonic NOIR. This stands for nominal, ordinal, interval and ratio data scales.

questions.stem: Which of the following scales of data measurement do blood groups belong?
questions.explanation: Bloods groups are nominal scale data or categorical data. This is because they are just labels and have no numerical value or meaningful order.

questions.stem: Which of the following are examples of nominal scale data?
questions.explanation:

There is no meaningful order or quantifiable variable in this kind of data. It is arranged on the basis of labels, titles or categories.
Kuppuswamy scale is an ordinal scale data. It is a scale representing socio-economic data.
Height is a ratio scale data as it can be arranged in a meaningful order with a well-defined size interval.

questions.stem: A physician classifies a group of patients based on disease severity as normal, mild, moderate and severe. Which of the following scales of data does this classification system belong to?
questions.explanation: The classification of this disease as normal, mild, moderate and severe belongs to the ordinal scale. This is because this arrangement is not only qualitative but also has a meaningful order with no interval in between.

questions.stem: Which of the following are representative of ordinal scale data?
questions.explanation:
TNM staging, Likert scale and severity of pain are measured on the ordinal scale.
In such cases, the arrangement is qualitative, with a meaningful order but there is no way of quantifying the difference between the individual variables. For example, grading of pain as mild, moderate, and severe.
The Likert scale is used in collecting self-reported data in questionnaire-based research. It is a psychometric scale used to understand people’s attitudes from responses. Usually, a 5-point scale of agreement is used which includes:
1 – Strongly disagree
2 – Disagree
3 – Neither agree nor disagree
4 – Agree
5 – Strongly agree
TNM staging is done for the staging of cancer. It is based on tumor size, lymph node status and metastasis. Lower stages indicate better prognosis than higher stages.
Hemoglobin level is an example of ratio scale data.
HIV positive or negative status falls under the category of nominal scale data.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a continuous variable?
options: Blood glucose value of a diabetic patient
Number of visits to the hospital in a year
questions.explanation:
The number of visits to the hospital in a year is a discrete variable. The only values it can take are whole numbers and none in between. For example, you can’t visit the hospital 2.5 times.
Blood glucose value, mid-arm circumference and birth weight are continuous variables. They can have any value within a limit or a range.

questions.stem: Match the following.
questions.explanation:
The number of cancer patients in a hospital is an example of discrete data. They can only take certain values and none in between.
The temperature measured in the Celsius scale is an example of interval scale data. Such data are arranged in a meaningful order but they can not have an absolute zero value. For example, 80 degree celcius to not twice as hot as 40 degree celcius and 0 degree celcius does not indicate an absolute abscence of heat.
Height and weight, blood pressure and temperature in the Kelvin scale are examples of ratio scale data. Such data are arranged in a meaningful order and the scales they are measured in have absolute zero value. For example, a temperature of 0 kelvin indicates an absolute abscense of heat.
Height and weight, blood pressure, and temperature are examples of continuous data as they can take any values between limits or a range.

Box plots may also have lines extending vertically from the boxes (i.e., whiskers) indicating variability outside the upper and lower quartiles. Hence, they are also known as box-and-whisker plots and box-and-whisker diagrams.

In this case, a tree diagram would help the doctor in explaining the possible outcomes to the patient’s diabetes, with the perspective of joint involvement.

questions.explanation:
The given image is of a histogram. It is used to represent frequency distributions of continuous quantitative data.
Nominal and ordinal data can be represented by a bar chart.

questions.stem: Which of the following can be used to represent quantitative data?
questions.explanation:
An ogive, a line diagram and a histogram can be used to represent quantitative data. The images shown above are:
A – Ogive
B – Bar graph
C – Line diagram
D – Histogram
Quantitative data cannot be represented by a bar graph. It is used mostly for nominal scale or qualitative data.

chapters.title: Descriptive Statistics II - Measures of Location

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a measure of location?
questions.explanation:
Percentile is a measure of position. It can be defined as a number that states the percentage of observations that fall below any particular score.
Measures of location help in summarizing the data by locating its centre or middle. The three main measures of location include mean, median and mode. They are also called measures of central tendency.

questions.stem: The mean can be calculated only if data is on:
questions.explanation:
The mean can be worked out only for quantitative values. Thus, it can be calculated for interval or ratio scale data.
A dichotomous scale is a type of nominal scale data that can take only two values. Example: Male/ Female. For nominal scale data, the preferred measure of central tendency is mode. For ordinal scale data, both median and mode can be calculated.
Median can be derived from ordinal, interval and ratio data scales. Mode can be derived from all scales of data- nominal, ordinal, interval and ratio.

questions.stem: During a school health survey on malnutrition, the children are arranged according to ascending order of their heights. Which of the following can be obtained by this arrangement?
questions.explanation:
The 50th centile can be obtained when values are arranged in order and the central value is picked out. This is the same as the median.
In a distribution that has an odd number of elements, the median is the middle value.
In a distribution that has an even number of elements, the median is the average of the middle values, i.e., the arithmetic mean of the two middle values.
An example of how to calculate the median of an odd and an even number of elements is given below.
[[IMG:1]]
[[IMG:2]]
[[IMG:3]]
Option C: Geometric mean is obtained by taking the arithmetic mean of values on a logarithmic scale.
Option D: Mean deviation is a measure of dispersion. The average of deviations from the arithmetic mean gives the mean deviation.

questions.stem: Which of the following can have more than one value?
questions.explanation:
The mode of a given sample can have more than one value. It is the most frequently occurring value in a distribution.
For example, in the sample [1, 3, 6, 6, 6, 6, 7, 7, 12, 12, 17], the most repeated value i.e., the mode
is 6.
For the list of data [1, 1, 2, 4, 4], the mode is 1 and 4. Therefore, the mode is not unique. This dataset may be said to be bimodal, while a set with more than two modes may be described as multimodal.
Median can have only one value, obtained by arranging values in order and then picking out the central value. In a sample with an even number of elements, median is obtained by taking the average of the middle 2 elements.
Mean can only have a single value. The harmonic mean is the reciprocal of the arithmetic mean of the reciprocals of the data values. The geometric mean is obtained by taking the arithmetic mean of values on a logarithmic scale.
813

questions.stem: While collecting data on which of the following variables would median not be the preferred measure of central tendency?
questions.explanation:
Blood pressure usually forms a normal symmetrical distribution for which mean is the preferred measure of central tendency.
Distributions of survival time, incubation period and health expenses have the probability of having extreme values, i.e., outliers. Thus, they form skewed distributions and in such cases, median is the preferred measure of central tendency.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true for the given distribution of ages of patients who are visiting a family planning clinic in a day?
questions.explanation:
The arithmetic mean from the following data is given by the sum of all the values, 270 divided by the number of values, 9 = 30.
The data can be arranged in ascending order as 20, 25, 28, 31, 31, 31, 31, 35, 38.
After arranging in order, the median is obtained by picking out the central value which is 31. The mode is the most frequently occurring value, which is 31 here.

questions.stem: You are conducting a study on birth weights in your hospital. Out of 11 births, 5 babies weighed over 2.5 kg, one baby weighed 2.5 kg and 5 weighed less than 2.5 kg. What does the value 2.5 represent in this distribution?
questions.explanation:
Out of the 11 birth weights, 2.5 kg would represent the middle value or the median. 5 babies weigh more than 2.5 kg and 5 less than that.
This can be understood from the image below.
[[IMG:1]]
Option A: Mean or arithmetic mean is the average value. In this case, the mean is the average of all the 11 values. It need not be 2.5.
Option B: Geometric mean is obtained by taking the arithmetic mean of values on a logarithmic scale.
Option D: ˜uartile is a measure of position, where the data is divided into four equal sets. 3/4 of the values are below the 3rd quartile reading. Hence, it cannot be the central reading.

questions.stem: You are conducting an epidemiological study on malaria in a town ç. The number of cases reported during the last 10 years is given below. What is the most appropriate measure of central tendency for this data?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, median is the preferred measure of central tendency as there are outliers.
The value of 5000 is an outlier in the given set, i.e., an observed value which is very distant from other observations in the distribution. This indicates the usage of median as the measure of central tendency as it is not sensitive to extreme values, unlike the mean.
By arranging the data in order: 100, 160, 190, 250, 260, 300, 320, 320, 350, 5000, we get the
median as (260 + 300) / 2 = 280.
Options A and B: Mean is the most affected by the presence of outliers. Mode is the least affected by outliers but it is used mainly for measuring the central tendency of nominal data.
Option D: Geometric mean can be used for datasets with extreme values but it is not used when the values can be zero or negative. In the given scenario, the number of malaria cases reported in a town can also have a zero value.

questions.stem: During a school health assessment, the mean value of weight for a group of 10 boys was found to be 18.2 kg. Žater, it was found that the weight of one of the boys was wrongly recorded as 2.0 kg instead of 20 kg. What is the true mean weight of the group?
questions.explanation:
The true mean weight of the group is 20 kg.
Mean is given as x■ = x / n, where n is the number of elements and x denotes the sum of all the elements in the series.
In this scenario, the incorrect mean is 18.2, i.e.,
x / 10 = 18.2, making x = 182.
But this is incorrect as one of the 10 weights was wrongly recorded as 2 instead of 20. The corrected x = (Incorrect x – incorrect value) + correct value.
The incorrect sum of all elements = 182, incorrect value =2 and the correct value = 20. Thus, the correct sum of all the 10 weights would be,
x = (182 – 2) + 20 = 200.
From this, the correct mean value of the 10 weights can be given by:
x / 10 = 200/ 10 = 20.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is correct about the given distribution of ages of patients attending a geriatric medicine clinic?
questions.explanation:
For the given dataset, the modes are 70 and 76. The mode is the most frequently occurring value. It can have multiple values. In this scenario, the values 70 and 76 have been repeated twice.
Median of this distribution is the central value, (76 + 80) / 2 = 78.

questions.stem: The smoking history for the past 6 years of a patient with emphysema is given in the table below. If a pack has 20 cigarettes, what is the mean, median and mode of the given data?
questions.explanation:
The distribution in this scenario in terms of the number of cigarettes smoked is 5, 10, 10, 10, 20, 40.
The mean here is x/n = 95/6 = 15.833 rounded off to 16.
The median here is the central value = average of 3rd and 4th values since the distribution has an even number of values. This comes to (10 + 10) / 2 = 10.
The mode here is 10 which has a frequency of 3 in the given dataset.

questions.stem: While reviewing a data distribution, you find that the highest value of 58 was wrongly recorded as 85 and so you correct it. How will this correction change the measures of central tendency?
options: No change in mean, decreased median
Decreased mean, no change in median
questions.explanation:
The given change in a dataset would cause a decrease in the mean but the median would remain unchanged.
The mean is sensitive to every value in the distribution. Since the correct value of 58 is much lesser than the wrongly recorded value of 85, the final mean will be decreased compared to the earlier recorded value.
However, as only the highest value was wrongly recorded, the median i.e., the central value, will remain the same.

questions.stem: While conducting a study on the age at death in males of a population Y, the distribution curve given below is obtained. Which of the following is true? [[IMG:1]]
questions.explanation:
The given image shows a negatively skewed or a left-skewed distribution curve. Here, mean <
median < mode.
Mode is the most frequently occurring value in the distribution and is given by the highest point of the graph. Since the given graph has only one peak, it is unimodal.
A positively skewed distribution refers to a right-skewed distribution. In such cases, mean >
median > mode.

questions.stem: Which of the following sets of measures of central tendency is likely to match the distribution depicted in the given image? [[IMG:1]]
questions.explanation:
The given image is of a right-skewed or positively skewed distribution. So, among the given options, the most likely values of mean = 3, median = 2, and mode = 1.
We can tell the direction of skew of a distribution by observing the direction of the tail. Here, the tail of the distribution is towards the positive direction and thus it is positively skewed
or right-skewed. In a positively skewed distribution, mean > median > mode.
If the tail of the distribution is towards the negative direction, the distribution would be negatively skewed or left-skewed. In such distributions, mode > median > mean.

questions.stem: You are conducting a study on blood pressure in a population. The systolic blood pressure values have a mean of 130 mmHg, a median of 140 mmHg and mode of 160 mmHg. What type of distribution is this?
questions.explanation:
This is a unimodal negatively skewed distribution.
In this scenario, the mean of 130 mmHg is less than the median of 140 mmHg which is less than mode of 160mmHg. Since mean<median<mode, this is an asymmetrical negatively skewed or left-skewed distribution.
It is a unimodal distribution as there is only a single value for mode. In a symmetrical distribution, the mean = median = mode.
In a positively skewed distribution, mean > median > mode.

questions.stem: The mean of a dataset is 2 and the median is 3. What is the mode?
questions.explanation:
As the mean  median, this is an asymmetric distribution and so we can use the formula: Mode = 3 median - 2 mean.
Using the given values, mode = (3x3) – (2x2) = 9 – 4 = 5.
A distribution is termed symmetric when the mean, median and mode coincide i.e., mean= median= mode.

questions.stem: Study A(red) and Study B(blue) done in a given population yields two different distribution curves as shown below. Comparing both the curves, which of the following will be true? [[IMG:1]]
options: Mean = median, not equal to mode
Mode = median, not equal to mean
questions.explanation:
On comparing the 2 graphs, we can say mean=median for both study A and B but the mode is different.
Study A is a unimodal symmetrical distribution, so mean=median=mode.
Study B is a bimodal distribution. Here, mean=median, but the curve has two highest points, therefore it has 2 modes.

chapters.title: Descriptive Statistics III - Measures of Dispersion

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a measure of dispersion?
questions.explanation:
Z scores are not a measure of dispersion, they are measures of position. It indicates the position of any element in a distribution in terms of how many standard deviations it lies from the mean of the distribution.
The most common measures of spread/dispersion are range, standard deviation and variance. They help in determining the extent to which data is stretched/scattered or squeezed/clustered.
They are also called measures of spread or scatter or variability.

questions.stem: What is standard deviation a measure of?
questions.explanation: Standard deviation is a measure of spread or dispersion or variability. Range and variability are other measures of spread.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the correct relationship between variance and standard deviation?
options: Variance = square root of standard deviation
Standard deviation = square root of variance
questions.explanation: Standard deviation is the square root of variance.

questions.stem: You are conducting a study on chronic kidney disease in a population. Your sample size is 28. What formula for standard deviation will you use here?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, the sample size is 28, which is <30. For a small sample, usually less than 30, the formula for standard deviation used is:
[[IMG:1]]
It is better to use n-1 in the denominator in the case of a small sample. But in the case of a very large sample subtracting 1 from a huge number will not make much of a significant correction. In those cases, we may choose to ignore subtracting 1.

questions.stem: Which among the following is true about standard deviation?
options: …ne standard deviation covers 95% of the values
It can be used only in normal distributions
It is a measure of central tendency
questions.explanation:
The standard deviation (S.D) indicates the distribution of variables. It is a measure of dispersion.
It can be used in normal and skewed distributions, but it is particularly useful in normal distributions.
1 S.D covers 68% of the values. 2 S.D covers 95% of the values. Measures of central tendency are mean, median and mode.

questions.stem: You are using the ‰uppuswamy scale to calculate the socio-economic status of 10 families in the railway staff quarters. You find that every family has a total monthly income of Rs. ‹3,355. What is the standard deviation of this sample?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, the standard deviation will be zero.
The monthly income of every family is Rs. ‹3,355. So, all the elements in this distribution are the same. Hence, there is no variability. Both the standard deviation and variance which is the square of standard deviation will be zero.

questions.stem: çach value of a study sample is multiplied by 10. What would be the new standard deviation of the observations?
questions.explanation:
When each element of a sample is multiplied by 10, the new standard deviation= 10 x original standard deviation.
The formula for standard deviation, SD = (x - x■)2/n-1.
If each element of the distribution is multiplied by 10, the new mean will become 10 times the original mean.
If all observations are multiplied by 10, then the new SD = (10x-10x■)2/n-1
= 10 (x - x■)2/n-1
= 10 x …riginal SD
Change in variance: variance = square of standard deviation, so when SD becomes 10 times, the variance will be 10² = 100 times the original variance.

questions.stem: …n plotting the blood pressure values of a population on a graph, you obtain the curve given below. Which of the following is true? [[IMG:1]]
questions.explanation:
The given image shows a normal distribution, also called bell curve or ™aussian distribution. It has no skew. It is defined by the mean and standard deviation. In a normal distribution, mean = median = mode.
The total area under the curve of a normal distribution is 1.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about the standard normal distribution?
questions.explanation: A standard normal distribution is a type of normal distribution. It is bell-shaped, has a mean of 0 and a standard deviation of 1. Thus the variance, the square of standard deviation is also 1 = the standard deviation.

questions.stem: In a normal curve, what is the percentage of distribution of one standard deviation?
questions.explanation:
Approximately 68% of a normal distribution falls within ±1 standard deviations of the mean. This is as per the empirical rule of a normal distribution.
Approximately 95% of the distribution falls within ±2 standard deviations of the mean. Approximately 99.‹% of the distribution falls within ±3 standard deviations of the mean.

questions.stem: During a study on anaemia in a population, a normal distribution curve with a mean of 13.5 g% is obtained. What proportion of the population constitutes people with haemoglobin values above 13.5 g%?
questions.explanation: In this scenario, 0.50, i.e., 50% of the population would have haemoglobin more than the mean, i.e., 13.5 gm%. In a normal distribution, 50% of the values lie above the mean.

questions.stem: The I’ scores of your study population form a bell-shaped curve. How much of the population falls between the median (Mdn) and Mdn + 1 S.D?
questions.explanation:
34% or 0.34 of the population in a normal distribution falls between the median and median plus one standard deviation.
The I’ values form a bell-shaped curve, which is seen in normal symmetric distributions.
According to the empirical rule of normal distributions, 68% of the distribution falls within 1 standard deviation of the mean, i.e., mean ± 1 SD covers 68% of the distribution.
šow, in a normal distribution, mean = median. Therefore, this 68% includes values from median
-1SD to median +1SD.
The question asks about the percentage that falls under median +1SD, which would be half of 68%, that is 34% or 0.34.

questions.stem: The fasting blood glucose levels of adults in a population forms a normal distribution. The statistical measures obtained are given below. Within what limits would 95% of the population have their blood glucose values?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, 95% of the population would have their blood sugar within the limits of 85 and 125 mg. Here, the mean blood sugar is 105 mg and the standard deviation is 10 mg.
According to the empirical rule of normal distribution, 95% of the distribution falls within two standard deviations of the mean.
In this question, 2 S.D = 10 x 2 = 20. We do, + and - 2 S.D from the mean to arrive at the limits within which 95% of the population would have their blood sugar, i.e., 85 and 125 mg.
+ and - 1 S.D = 10 from the mean, we get the limits within which 68% of the population would have their blood sugar value, i.e., 95 and 115 mg.
+ and - 3 S.D = 30, from the mean, we get limits within which 99% would have their values, i.e.,
‹5 and 135 mg.

questions.stem: The peak expiratory flow rate (PçFR) values of a group of 11-year-old girls have a mean of 300 l/min and a standard deviation of 20 l/min. What are the deviation scores for the PçFR values of two girls recorded as 280 l/min and 330 l/min respectively?
questions.explanation:
The deviation scores for PçFR values 280 l/min and 330 l/min are -20 and 30 respectively.
The Deviation score of an element in a distribution is the difference between the mean of the distribution and the element itself, i.e., it is obtained by subtracting the distribution’s mean from the element.
Applying this here, deviation score of the value 280 l/min = the element - the mean = 280 - 300 =
-20.
For the value 330 l/min, deviation score = 330 - 300 = 30.

questions.stem: The shape of a normal distribution curve depends on?
questions.explanation:
The shape of a normal distribution curve depends upon its mean and standard deviation.
For example, for a particular mean value, a smaller standard deviation value gives a taller and narrower curve whereas, a larger value gives a flatter curve.
The curve is centered at the mean  which coincides with the median and the mode and is located at the point beneath the peak of the curve. The mean, median and mode are equal.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a property of a normal distribution curve?
questions.explanation:
In a normal distribution curve, mean = median.
mean > median in positively/ rightward skewed distribution. mean < median in negatively/ leftward skewed distribution.

questions.stem: Which of the following is incorrect about the standard normal distribution?
questions.explanation: In a standard normal distribution, mean = 0.

questions.stem: A population study showed a mean glucose of 86 mg/dL. In a sample of 100 showing normal distribution, what percentage of people will have blood glucose above 86 mg/dL?

In a normal distribution, 50% of the values lie above the mean.

questions.stem: The mean value of marks in a distribution of 100 students in a class is 105 and standard deviation is 10. How many students will have their marks between 85 and 125?
questions.explanation:

questions.stem: The systolic blood pressure of a group of normal people between the ages of 25–2‹ years was taken and a mean of 120 mmHg was found. What will be the expected number of individuals among a group of 100 people taken for the study whose BP will be below 120 mmHg?
questions.explanation:
In a normal distribution, 50% of the values lie below the mean.
In this scenario, 50%, i.e., 50 of the 100 people will have a systolic BP of less than 120 mmHg.

questions.stem: In a normal distribution, what percentage of the distribution falls within 2 standard deviations of the mean?
questions.explanation: According to the empirical rule of normal distributions, 95% of the distribution falls within 2 standard deviations of the mean, i.e., mean ± 2 SD covers 95% of the distribution.
