68% of the population will lie between 180- 220.
In a normal distribution curve, 68% of the values lie within the mean +/- 1 standard deviation and the mean=median=mode. Since the mean = 200 and the standard deviation = 20:
68% of population will lie between Mean +/- 1SD, that is, 200 +/- 20 = 180-220 95% of population lies between Mean+/-2SD, 200+/- 2*20 = 160- 240
99% of population lies between Mean+/-3SD, 200+/- 3*20 = 140- 260

chapters.title: Descriptive Statistics IV - Measures of Position

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a measure of position?
questions.explanation:
Range is not a measure of position, it is a measure of dispersion or spread.
The most common measures of position are quantiles, quartiles, centiles and z-scores (standard scores). Measures of position give the position of specific data in relation to other data in the set.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about quantiles are true?
questions.explanation:
Quantiles are elements in a distribution that divide data into equal groups. They are also known as fractiles. Median divides a distribution into two equal parts, so it is considered as a quantile.
Quantiles are used for continuous, quantitative data.
Quintiles are a type of quantile that divides data into 5 equal groups.

questions.stem: Centiles divide data into equal parts?
questions.explanation: Centiles divide data into 100 equal parts.

questions.stem: During a school health camp, a group of 250 students are arranged in the ascending order of their height. Which student would have the 40th percentile value for height?
questions.explanation:
Here, the 100th student will have the 40th percentile value for height. To arrive at this, we use the formula R = P/100 x (n + 1).
where R is the rank of the desired observation, P is the quantile/percentile desired and n is the number of variables in the data.
Thus, R = 40/100 x (250 + 1) = 0.4 x 251 = 100.4.
This is rounded up to the closest number making R = 100.

questions.stem: By calculating which of the following can we obtain the central value of a sample with 180 elements?
questions.explanation:
The 2nd quartile gives the central value of 180 elements. The central value of a distribution is given by the median. It divides the distribution into the ratio of 1:1.
In quartiles elements of the distribution are divided into 4 equal parts by 3 values. Each part contains a quarter, i.e., 25% of the values. So two quarters would give half of the values. So the element present at the position of the 2nd quartile would be the central value, i.e., the median, with half the values before and half the values after it. This is shown in the image given below.
[[IMG:1]]
The 5th decile and 50th percentile represent the median values of a distribution in decile and percentile respectively.

questions.stem: Which measure of position divides the distribution in a ratio of 3:1?
questions.explanation:
Third quartile Q3 divides the distribution into the ratio of 3:1.
In quartiles:
the first quartile Q1 divides the distribution in the ratio of 1:3
the second quartile Q2 divides it in the ratio of 1:1.
The division of data by quartiles is shown in the below image.
[[IMG:1]]
Centiles divide data into 100 equal parts. 33rd centile divides the distribution in the ratio of 33:67. Deciles divide data into 10 equal parts. 7th decile divides the distribution in the ratio of 7:3.

questions.stem: ‰ou are recording the blood pressure values of 200 adults in a population. The first quartile diastolic BP is 68 mmHg and the third quartile is 105 mmHg. How many patients are there in the 3rd and 4th quarters?
questions.explanation:
In a quartile, the data is divided into 4 equal parts, i.e., 4 quarters. Therefore, in this scenario, there are 50% of patients in the 3rd and 4th quarters, i.e 100 patients.
The division of data by quartiles is shown in the image given below.
[[IMG:1]]
[[IMG:2]]

questions.stem: The forced expiratory volume (FEV) of 300 patients visiting the respiratory medicine outpatient department is recorded. The data has a median value of 2.5 litres with the first and third quartiles being 1.5 litres and 4.5 litres respectively. How many persons in the sample are expected to have an FEV between 1.5 and 4.5 litres?
questions.explanation:
150 persons are expected to have FEV between 1.5 and 4.5 litres.
In a quartile, the data is divided by 3 values into 4 equal parts. Thus, each part will have 25% of the values in the distribution.
In this scenario, each part will have 75 persons. Here, 1.5 is the first quartile Q1, 2.5 is the second quartile Q2 and 4.5 is the third quartile Q3. Between Q1 and Q3 there are two quarters, thus there will be 150 people with FEV between 1.5 and 4.5 litres.
Data division by quartiles is shown in the below image.

questions.stem: Which of the following distributions is preferred for the calculation of z scores?
questions.explanation: Z scores are usually calculated in normal distributions.

questions.stem: In a study on haemoglobin levels in healthy women, the data recorded has a mean of 13.5 gm/dL and a standard deviation of 1.5 gm/dL. What is the z score for an element with a haemoglobin value of 15.0 gm/dL?
questions.explanation:
The Z score for the element with a haemoglobin value of 15 gm/dL is 1.0. The formula for z score, z = (X- µ)/.
X is the value of the element, µ is the mean and  is the standard deviation. In this scenario, z = (15 – 13.5) / 1.5 = 1.5/1.5 = 1.

questions.stem: The diastolic BP of 125 women aged between 18 and 60 years was recorded. The mean of the data is 70 mmHg with a standard deviation of 10 mmHg. What will be the 5th percentile value?
questions.explanation:
The z value for the 5th percentile is -1.645.
˜sing the formula for z scores, z = (X- µ)/, we get X = z + µ.
In this scenario, X = (-1.645 x 10) + 70 = -16.45 + 70 = 53.55 = 53.6.

questions.stem: The statistical methods that go further than merely summarizing data are a part of:
questions.explanation:
Inferential statistics are those statistical methods that go further than just summarizing data.
They involve inductive reasoning and using a statistic to estimate a parameter. E.g., the expected success rate of vasectomy or mean blood pressure of all Indians.
One of the most common problems faced in research is using information gathered by researching a sample and then drawing conclusions about the population from which the sample is drawn.
Here, sample statistics (sample mean and SD) are known and population parameters (population mean and SD) are unknown.
Inferential statistical methods are used to draw conclusions about the population parameters from sample statistics.

questions.stem: Which of the following measures relative variation between two different units?
questions.explanation: Co-efficient of variation (CV) measures the relative variability between two different units, by using the mean and standard deviation.

questions.stem: The weight of the 100 children that presented in the pediatric OPD in the last week was analyzed. The median weight was 12 kg and the standard deviation was 3. This data formed a normal distribution. What is the coefficient of variation?
questions.explanation:
In the given scenario, coefficient of variance (CV) = 25%.
Coefficient of variation, CV = standard deviation x 100/ mean = 3 x 100/12 = 25%. In a normal distribution, mean = median.

questions.stem: The means of all possible samples from a population are plotted on a linear graph. What is this called?
questions.explanation: The random sampling distribution of means is the distribution formed when all possible sample means from a population are plotted in a frequency distribution.

questions.stem: Central limit theorem is related to:
questions.explanation:
The central limit theorem is related to the random sampling distribution of means. According to this theorem, as the sample size increases:
The sampling distribution tends towards a normal distribution curve (bell curve)
Regardless of the population's actual distribution shape
Assuming all samples are identical in size
The sample mean and standard deviations become closer to the population mean and standard deviations

questions.stem: A researcher wanted to calculate the mean age of onset of type II diabetes mellitus in a population. He got a sample mean of 45. To measure the extent of deviation from the population mean, which of the following should he use?
questions.explanation: The standard error is a measure of the extent to which the sample means deviate from the true population means.

questions.stem: Standard deviation of mean measures variations caused by:
questions.explanation: The standard deviation of mean or standard error of means measures variations caused by sampling errors.

questions.stem: Consider a sample of 100 women with an average Hb of 10 g% and standard deviation of 1. What is the standard error of this sample?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, the standard error SE = 0.1. The formula for standard error:
SE = Standard deviation/ sample size =1/100 = 1/10 = 0.1

questions.stem: All of the following are true about standard error except:
options: It increases as the sample size increases.
It is based on a normal distribution
It depends on the standard deviation of means
It is used to estimate confidence limits
questions.explanation: As the sample size increases, the standard error will decrease, not increase. The standard error is inversely related to the square root of the sample size.

questions.stem: The incubation period for measles in a group of 25 children was calculated. Following findings were recorded. What is the standard error?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, the standard error = 0.4. The formula for standard error:
SE = Standard deviation/sample size = 2/25 = 2/5 = 0.4

questions.stem: The uppermost and lowermost values of standard errors within which a parameter value is expected to lie are called the:
questions.explanation:
The uppermost and lowermost limits of standard errors within which a parameter value is expected to lie are called the confidence limits.
The difference between upper and lower confidence limits is called the confidence interval.

questions.stem: Which of the following parameters are used to calculate the confidence limit?
questions.explanation: Confidence limits are calculated with the sample mean and standard error.

questions.stem: During screening of a population, the mean cholesterol levels were found to be 230mg/dL. The standard error was 10. Calculate the ‘5% confidence limits.
questions.explanation:
In the given scenario, ‘5% confidence limits are 210 – 250.
In inferential statistics, ‘5% confidence limits = Sample mean (x■) ± 2 standard errors.
In this case, mean is 230 and the standard error is 10. Hence, confidence limits are 210-250.

questions.stem: What is the hypothesis which states that an apparent effect is only due to chance, called as?
questions.explanation: The hypothesis that an apparent effect is only due to chance is a null hypothesis. If this is rejected as false, we have an alternative hypothesis.

questions.stem: What is the significance level in hypothesis testing called as?
questions.explanation: Significance level in hypothesis testing is called alpha level () or criterion.

questions.stem: What is the p value?
options: Probability of declaring a significant difference when there is none in reality
Probability of declaring a significant difference when it is actually present
Probability of not declaring a significant difference when actually it is not present
Probability of not declaring a significant difference when actually it is present
questions.explanation: p-value can be defined as the probability of declaring a significant difference when there is none in reality.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is false about the p-value?
options: It is equal to the probability of committing a type I error
It is the chance that the presence of difference is concluded when actually there may be none
When the p value is less than , the result is statistically significant
questions.explanation:
The power of a test is 1 – beta.
The p value is the probability that a type I error is being made. It is the chance that the presence of difference is concluded when actually there may be none. When the p value is less than , the result is statistically significant.

questions.stem: A randomized control trial comparing the efficacy of two chemotherapy regimens for Hodgkin's lymphoma showed that their difference is statistically significant with p < 0.001. However, in reality the two drugs do not differ in their efficacy. What type of error is this an example of?
questions.explanation:
This is an example of a type I error.
In this scenario, let us take the null hypothesis as the efficacy of two drugs being the same, which as the question states, is true in reality. The alternative hypothesis will then be that one drug is better than the other.
The questions states that p-value was found to be < 0.001, which is statistically significant and so the null hypothesis is rejected. But we already know that the null hypothesis is true and we are forced to accept the alternative hypothesis even though it is false.
When an alternative hypothesis is accepted even when it is false and the null hypothesis is true, it is called as a type I error or an alpha error or a false positive error.

questions.stem: An investigator is conducting a study to assess the effect of a mood stabiliser on patients with bipolar I disorder. What does it mean if the difference is significant in the results?
options: p > 0.05 and it is likely by chance
p > 0.05 and it is unlikely by chance
p < 0.05 and it is unlikely by chance
p < 0.05 and it is likely by chance
questions.explanation:
When the difference is significant, it means that the difference is unlikely by chance and p will be
 0.05.

questions.stem: While assessing the effect of a new intervention for type II DM, you obtain the p-value of the study as 0.023. Based on this observation, what is your inference?
options: Null hypothesis is accepted and the study is rejected
Null hypothesis is rejected and the study is accepted
Null hypothesis is accepted and the study is accepted
Null hypothesis is rejected and the study is also rejected
questions.explanation: By convention, if the p value  0.05, the difference is said to be statistically significant. Thus, the null hypothesis is rejected and the study is accepted.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a false statement regarding hypothesis testing?
options: Alpha is the maximum tolerable probability of a type 1 error being made
Beta is the probability of a type II error
When the null hypothesis is true but rejected, it is a type II error
p value can be more or less than alpha
questions.explanation: When the null hypothesis is true but is still rejected, it is a type I error and not a type II error. Type II errors are when an alternative hypothesis is rejected even though it is true.

questions.stem: You are conducting a randomised clinical trial to see if a new drug 'A' has better efficacy than the standard drug 'B', in patients with grade III hypertension. While analysing the results of this study, you conclude that no difference exists between the two. But in reality, a difference between them truly exists. What type of error are you making?
questions.explanation:
Type II errors are when an alternative hypothesis is rejected when it is true.
In this scenario, the null hypothesis is that there is no difference and the alternative hypothesis is that there is a difference.
We failed to reject the null hypothesis that says there is no difference, and so we are making a type II error. In other words, we have rejected the alternative hypothesis that there is an difference when it is true.

questions.stem: Power of a study is the ability of a test to
questions.explanation: The power of a study is its ability to avoid or decrease beta errors or type II errors. The statistical power of a test is represented by 1 – .

questions.stem: A randomised control trial is being conducted in patients with direct inguinal hernia, to compare the outcomes of a new surgery 'A' and the gold standard surgery 'B'. The p value of this trial is found to be 0.04. What can we conclude from this?
options: Type II error is small and we can accept the findings of the study
The probability of false negative conclusion that operation A is better than B is 4%
The power of the study to detect the difference between operation A and B is 96%
The probability of a false positive conclusion that operation A is better than B is 4%
questions.explanation:
Since the p-value of the study is found to be 0.04, we can infer that the probability of a false positive conclusion that the operation A is better than B is 4%.
In this scenario, the p value is 0.04 which makes it, by convention, statistically significant. We can reject the null hypothesis and accept the alternative hypothesis that operation A is better than
operation B.

questions.stem: You are an investigator conducting a statistical test. You obtain the p value as 0.01 for your study. What does this mean?
options: The probability of finding a significant difference is 1%
There is a 1% probability that the difference is not by chance
The difference is not significant 1% of times and significant 99% of times
The power of the test used is 99%
questions.explanation:
If the p-value = 0.01, then the difference is not significant 1% of the time and significant 99% of the time.
In other words, there is a 99% probability that the difference is not by chance and there is a 1% probability that the difference is only by chance.

questions.stem: In a well-designed cancer study, similar remission rates were obtained for a new treatment (33.2%) and the usual treatment (32.2%), with the p-value being 0.04. Which of the following statements is true regarding the study?
options: Both the treatments are equally effective
Neither of the treatments is effective
The new treatment is more effective than the usual treatment
The information given is not adequate to compare the efficacy of the treatments
questions.explanation:
As the p-value is 0.04, we can conclude that the new treatment is more effective than the usual treatment.
Even though both treatments have similar rates of remission, a valid statistical test is required to determine the difference in their effectiveness. Statistically, p-value < 0.05 implies that the alternate hypothesis is true.
In this scenario, we can consider:
Null hypothesis: Both the treatments are equally effective (in other terms, there is no difference between the effect of the two treatments).
Alternative hypothesis: New treatment is more effective than the usual treatment.
As the p-value is 0.04, which is statistically significant (<0.05), the null hypothesis is rejected and the alternative hypothesis is accepted. Hence the new treatment is more effective than the usual treatment.

questions.stem: Which of these tests is used in case of a nominal data?
questions.explanation:
Chi-square test deals with nominal/ non-parametric data (qualitative).
Nominal data is one with a name and does not have a numerical value. Ex blood group, gender, religion
Student's t test, ANOVA, and paired t test are used for parametric data (quantitative).

questions.stem: Which of the following is true for non-parametric tests?
options: ANOVA is an example of a non parametric test
It is used for skewed distributions
It involves the assumption that the data has a normal distribution
It cannot be used for small sample sizes
questions.explanation:
Non-parametric tests are tests that do not assume that the data is normally distributed. Thus, they are used for skewed (asymmetric) distributions {skewed either to the lesser side (left-sided skewed) or towards the greater side (right-sided skewed)}.
The chi-square test is an example of a non-parametric test that is used to test hypotheses in relation to nominal scale data or categorical data.
ANOVA is an example of a parametric test.

questions.stem: Which of these terms is used for paired t tests?
questions.explanation: Paired t tests are also called correlated pairs t test, paired samples t test, or dependent samples t test.

questions.stem: The test of significance done for two or more proportions:
questions.explanation:
Chi-Square(2) test is a test used for proportions and associations.
It is a non-parametric (non-numeric) test and it is used to test hypotheses in relation to nominal scale data or categorical data.

questions.stem: A researcher can use the chi-square test in all of the following situations, except:
options: To test the hypothesis that drug A has the same potency as drug B
To calculate the degree of freedom of a 3 x 4 contingency table
To compare the mean corpuscular volume in normal subjects versus those suffering from hereditary spherocytosis
To compare the proportions of overweight boys and girls in a class
questions.explanation:
The Chi-square test is not used for comparing means for different groups as means can only be calculated for quantitative data.
The Chi-square test is used for qualitative data. It can be used:
To test the null hypothesis
To compare proportions
To calculate the degree of freedom

questions.stem: Which of the following is not true about the Chi-square test?
options: Tests the significance of difference between two proportions
Tells about the presence or absence of an association between two variables
Directly measures the strength of association
It is usually used for skewed data
questions.explanation: A Chi-square test does not directly measure the strength of association. It merely tells about the presence or lack of association.

questions.stem: A Chi-square test would be most appropriate for testing which of the following hypotheses?
options: The mean AIPGE score of Chennai students is greater than Mumbai students
A smaller proportion of people who were immunized against chicken pox subsequently develop zoster than those who were not immunized
The mean BP of indian, american and english hypertensive men taking ACE inhibitors is the same as that of indian, american and english hypertensive women on ACEIs
The mean cost of treating a patient with CAD by angioplasty is greater than the mean cost of providing medical treatment
questions.explanation:
The Chi-square test is used to compare proportions or qualitative variables e.g., whether people developed zoster or not.
Options A and D: Two independent groups are being compared with quantitative variables (exam scores and cost, respectively). Thus, an unpaired t test will be used.
Option C: The blood pressure of 3 groups are being compared, thus making analysis of variance
(ANOVA) the most appropriate method of testing significance.

questions.stem: The test of choice to measure the difference in means between two groups in a study, with one group being a control is:
questions.explanation: The test of choice to measure the difference in means between two groups in a study, with one group being a control is unpaired T test.

questions.stem: A cardiologist wants to study the effect of the atorvastatin drug. She measures the initial cholesterol levels of 50 patients. After a month's treatment, she measures the cholesterol level again. Which of the following tests will she use to test the statistical significance of the change in the cholesterol level?
questions.explanation: In this scenario, the variable (cholesterol level) is quantitative. Moreover, the comparison is being done before and after the treatment (dependent). Hence, a paired t test will be used.

questions.stem: In a particular trial, the association of lung cancer with smoking is found to be 40% in one sample and 60% in another. What is the best test to compare the results?
questions.explanation: Chi-square tests are best used in comparing proportions and associations.

questions.stem: A pediatrician carried out a study to assess the difference in growth velocities in boys and girls. The average height of a group of 20 boys aged 10 years was 140 ± 13 cm and for 20 girls of the same age was 135 ± 7 cm. To test the statistical significance of the difference in height, which test would she use?
questions.explanation: In the given scenario, two independent groups are being compared with quantitative variables. Thus, a student t test or unpaired t-test is used.

questions.stem: A clinical trial was done between two groups to measure their blood pressure after treatment. Which of the following tests would be appropriate to use?
questions.explanation:
In the given scenario, two groups are being compared independent of each other. Hence, students t test/ unpaired t test should be used.
T tests are used if 2 groups are being compared. If the same group is compared before and after, paired T test is used. Otherwise, unpaired T test is used.

questions.stem: Analysis of variance test is used in which scenario among the following?
options: Comparing proportions in more than 2 groups
Comparing means in more than 2 groups
Comparing means in same groups before and after intervention
Comparing means in less than or equal to 2 groups
questions.explanation: Analysis of variance or ANOVA is used when more than 2 groups are compared for a quantitative difference (means).

questions.stem: A study was done to assess nutritional status among young children in rural and urban areas. 30 children in rural and 20 children in urban areas were malnourished. Which of the following tests of significance is the most appropriate in this case?
questions.explanation:
The most appropriate test of significance, in this case, is the chi-square test. It is used to compare qualitative data between 2 groups with independent measures.
Option B: Paired t-test compares paired data or pre-intervention and post-intervention data of the same group. This doesn't apply here as the groups are not paired.
Option C: The standard error of the mean is calculated for quantitative data, with a measure of central tendency as mean.
Option D: ANOVA is used to compare more than 2 groups.

questions.stem: A study was conducted to compare the incidence of postpartum depression in mothers as compared to the sex of the child. For assessment, Edinburg Depression scaled score (EDSS) was used. The study was divided into mothers with male babies as one group to be compared with mothers with female babies. Which of the following statistical test will be used to determine the association?
questions.explanation:
The Chi-square test is used to compare qualitative data and compares 2 groups with independent measures. The variables used here are yes/no signifying the presence/absence of postpartum depression. Hence it is the most appropriate test here.
Option A: Student’s t-test is for quantitative data. Here the data is qualitative, hence it can't be used.
Option B: Paired t-test compares paired data or pre-intervention and post-intervention data of the same group. This doesn't apply here as the groups are not paired.
Option C: ANOVA is used to compare more than 2 groups.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate test for testing the statistical significance of the difference in heights of school children?
questions.explanation:
Analysis of variance or ANOVA is used when more than 2 variable groups are compared.
In the scenario of comparing heights of school children, we would divide the school children into classes or grades or sections or by schools themselves, etc. This would involve comparing more than 2 groups and thus ANOVA is used.
Remember if the question limits its comparison within 2 groups, for example, comparison between boys and girls in a class then we have to choose unpaired t test.

questions.stem: An investigator wants to study the association between maternal intake of iron supplements and the incidence of low birth weight. He collects relevant data from 100 pregnant women regarding the status of usage of iron supplements and the status of birth weight in their newborns. Which of the following tests will he use for his study?
questions.explanation:
Here, two qualitative variables are being evaluated. First, whether the child belongs to the low birth weight category or not (and not the actual weight of the child, which is a quantitative value). Second, whether or not the mother took iron supplements in the gestational period. Hence,
the chi-square test is used as the test the significance of the association.

questions.stem: In a study, two groups of newborns are checked for differences in their birth weights based on whether mothers received supplements or not. Which of the following would be most appropriate test of significance?
questions.explanation: The unpaired t-test is used to test the difference between two groups of parametric variables or means when the samples are independent of each other. Here, birth weights (quantitative variable) of the two groups of newborns are being compared, which are independent of each other.

questions.stem: A study was planned to find out the effect of iron supplementation during pregnancy on the birth weight of newborn children. Two groups, one with iron supplementation and the other without, were compared. Birth weights of newborns were recorded as means + SD. Which statistical test is appropriate for the comparison of birth weights between the two groups?
questions.explanation: In the given scenario, we aim to compare only the birth weights of the two groups, which is a quantitative data, and thus an unpaired t test is most appropriate.

questions.stem: While applying the Chi-square test to a contingency table of 4 rows and 4 columns, what would the degree of freedom be in this case?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, df = (4 – 1) (4 – 1) = 9.
In a Chi-square test for a contingency table, the degrees of freedom (df) = (r-1) (c-1), where r is the number of rows and c is the number of columns.

questions.stem: In a Chi-square test for the following data, the degrees of freedom will be: [[IMG:1]]
questions.explanation:
In this scenario,contingency table has 3 rows and 4 columns. Hence, the degree of freedom, df = (3 – 1) (4 – 1) = 6.
In a Chi-square test for a contingency table, the degrees of freedom (df) = (r-1) (c-1), where r is the number of rows and c is the number of columns.

questions.stem: A study is conducted to find the relationship between the height and weight of school students. Which of the following would be useful in this study?
questions.explanation:
The coefficient of correlation can be used to determine the relationship between both variables in this scenario. It is used to express the strength and direction of the relationship between two variables.
It is represented by the letter 'r'. Its value ranges from -1 to +1.

questions.stem: Which among the following is false about correlation?
options: It indicates the strength of relationship between 2 variables
Correlation coefficient of 1 indicates a linear relationship
questions.explanation:
A correlation between 2 variables only indicates the strength of the relationship between two variables, not causation.
A correlation coefficient of 1 indicates a linear relationship. It cannot measure the risk.

questions.stem: During a study conducted to assess the effect of smoking on life expectancy, the correlation coefficient was found to be 0.60. Calculate the coefficient of determination for this study.
questions.explanation:
The coefficient of determination (CD) for this study is 0.36 (36%).
It is calculated by r2, where r is the correlation coefficient. In this study, the correlation coefficient
(r) is 0.6.
Hence CD = (0.6)2 = 0.36
The coefficient of determination refers to the percentage variability in one variable due to a change in the other variable. In the above study, a coefficient of determination of 0.36 means that 36% of the variation in life expectancy is accounted for by smoking.

questions.stem: What is the best way to study relationship between two variables?
questions.explanation:
A scattergram/ scatter plot is the best way to study the relationship between 2 variables. The following image shows a scatter plot.
[[IMG:1]]
[[IMG:2]]
The following image shows a forest plot.
The following image shows a funnel plot.
[[IMG:3]]
[[IMG:4]]
The following image shows a frequency polygon.

questions.stem: A psychiatry resident is conducting a study to assess the relationship between prefrontal blood flow under cognitive load and the severity of psychotic symptoms in schizophrenic patients. He calculates the correlation coefficient as -1.24. You can therefore conclude that:
options: Prefrontal blood flow is a good predictor of the severity of psychotic symptoms
Prefrontal blood flow accounts for most of the variance in symptoms
Schizophrenia causes low prefrontal blood flow
The correlation coefficient has been calculated incorrectly
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, the correlation coefficient (r) of -1.24 is incorrect, as 'r' can only lie between -1 to
+1.

questions.stem: In a random sample of 5000 corporate workers, the correlation coefficient of work satisfaction and life expectancy was found to be +0.7 with a p-value of 0.01. What is your interpretation?
options: Work satisfaction does not improve life expectancy
Strong statistically significant positive association between the variables
70% people who enjoy work will live longer
30% people who do not enjoy work will have a shorter life expectancy
questions.explanation:
The above study is statistically significant (p-value = 0.01) and indicates a strong positive correlation (correlation coefficient = +0.7) between work satisfaction and life expectancy.
Correlation is a measure of the statistical association of the variables, not a causal relationship.
Here, the coefficient of determination (r2) = 0.7 x 0.7 = 0.49. This means that 49% of the variation in life expectancy can be explained by satisfaction at work.

questions.stem: A group of cardiologists found a correlation coefficient of 0.90 (p-value = 0.01) between the systolic BP and serum cholesterol levels of patients attending their clinics. Which of the following statements is an incorrect interpretation of this study?
options: The magnitude of systolic BP and serum cholesterol levels are closely related
A patient with a high systolic BP is likely to have high serum cholesterol
A patient with a low systolic BP is likely to have low serum cholesterol
80% of the variation in BP can be explained by serum cholesterol and vice versa
questions.explanation:
Correlation is an indicator of the strength and direction of the relationship between 2 variables, not the magnitude.
The given study is statistically significant (p-value = 0.01) with a strong positive correlation (r =
+0.90) between systolic BP and cholesterol levels. Thus, it is likely that patients with high systolic BP will have high cholesterol levels and those with low BP will have low cholesterol levels.
The coefficient of determination (r2)here is 0.9 x 0.9 = 0.81. This indicates that around 80% of the variation in systolic BP among the patients can be explained by serum cholesterol levels.

questions.stem: Among the given options, what can be the likely value of the coefficient of correlation between infant mortality rate and economic status?
questions.explanation:
Among the given options, the coefficient of correlation between infant mortality rate and economic status (r) is likely to be -0.8.
It is known that low economic status is associated with a high infant mortality rate. This indicates a negative correlation. However, the infant mortality rate is also influenced by other factors, indicating a moderate correlation (not equal to 1). This makes -0.8 the most likely value of correlation.

questions.stem: High salt intake in individuals is associated with high blood pressure. What type of correlation is this?
questions.explanation:
An increase in blood pressure with salt intake is an example of a positive correlation.
The association of decreased life expectancy with increased smoking is an example of negative correlation.

questions.stem: A scattergram was plotted as shown below to study the relationship between two variables. What is the correct interpretation? [[IMG:1]]
options: There is correlation between both variables and the Pearson’s coefficient is 1
There is correlation between both variables and the Pearson’s coefficient is – 1
There is non-linear correlation between both variables
There is no association between both variables
questions.explanation:
The given scattergram depicts a non-linear correlation between the two variables.
Correlation expresses the strength and direction of the relationship between two variables in terms of a correlation coefficient. There are two types of correlation coefficients:
Pearson coefficient | Spearman coefficient
Used for data withcontinuous intervals | Used for data withdiscrete or deredintervals
Pearson coefficient	Spearman coefficient | Pearson coefficient	Spearman coefficient
Used to findlinearrelationshi ps(e.g. salt intake vs blood pr essure) | Used to findlinearornon-linea rrelationships(e.g. socioecono mic status vs parity)

questions.stem: What conclusion can be drawn from the following scattergram? [[IMG:1]]
options: There is a perfect negative correlation between the two variables
There is a high positive correlation between the two variables
There is a high negative correlation between the two variables
There is a perfect positive correlation between the two variables
questions.explanation: The given scattergram shows a high negative correlation between the two variables.

questions.stem: The value of one parameter can be estimated from another related parameter by:
questions.explanation: The value of one parameter can be estimated from another related parameter by using regression techniques.

questions.stem: If correlation is given by the equation y = a + bx, what would be the nature of the graph?
questions.explanation: The equation, y = a + bx indicates a straight line.

questions.stem: Look at the image below and select the linear regression equation corresponding to the graph. [[IMG:1]]
questions.explanation:
Among the given options, the equation y=11+2x corresponds to the linear regression equation of the form y= + x.
When 2 variables are correlated, such that the dependent variable is represented on the y-axis and the independent variable on the x-axis, then the value of y can be obtained by using the linear regression equation y =  + x, where:
y - dependent variable
 - intercept
 - slope of the line
x - independent variable
In the equation y=11+2x, the intercept() = 11, while the slope of the line () = 2.
Option A: y=10-x, represents an intercept of 10, and a slope of -1 indicating a negative correlation. However, the given image shows a positive correlation.
Options B and D: They do not fit the linear regression equation of the form y =  + x.

questions.stem: In a study, the total cholesterol was calculated as a + b■x■ + b■x■ + b■ x■, where x■ indicates calorie intake, x■ indicates physical activity, and x■ indicates body mass index. What is this an example of?
questions.explanation:
The given equation of y = a + b1x1 +b2x2…..bnxn is an example of multiple linear regression. In this equation:
b1, b2…..bn represent different regression coefficients x1, x2…….xn represent the known variables

questions.stem: An epidemiologist has determined five independent factors influencing the outcome of a particular disease. Which of the following statistical methods can he use to compare these factors?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, the outcome to be determined (dependent variable) is the occurrence of the disease, which is categorical (qualitative) in nature. Logistic regression can be used when a categorical dependent variable is being compared with either a categorical or numerical independent variable.
Linear regression is used when the outcome is numerical.
 | Dependent variable (outco me) |  | 
Independent variable(risk factors, exposure) |  | Qualitative (categorical) | Quantitative (numeric al)
Qualitative (categorical) | Logistic regressionChi-squ are | Linear regressionT-testA NOVA | 
Quantitative (numerical) | Logistic regression | Linear regression |

questions.stem: What test is used to compare Kaplan-Meier survival curves?
questions.explanation:
The Cox proportional hazards test is used to compare Kaplan-Meier survival curves.
Survival analysis is used for analyzing the expected duration of time until one event occurs, such as death. The following methods are used for this are:
Life table analysis
Kaplan-Meier analysis - it involves calculating the survival function (the probability that a person will survive past a certain time)
Life tables and survival functions are graphically represented in a Kaplan-Meier plot or curve.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not used to compare survival curves?
questions.explanation:
Fisher’s exact test is not used to compare survival curves. The following tests are used to compare the survival curves or Kaplan-Meier curves:
Mantel-Haenszel test
Log-rank test
Cox regression or Cox proportional hazards analysis

questions.stem: What is the Spearman coefficient used to determine?
questions.explanation:
Spearman coefficient is used to determine correlation. It is used to find linear or non-linear relationships for data with discrete ordered intervals.
Pearson correlation coefficient is used to find linear relationships for data with continuous intervals.

questions.stem: A researcher wants to compare a newly developed test for COVID with the gold standard test. Which of the following methods can he use?
questions.explanation: The Bland-Altmann analysis is used for comparing a newly developed test with another test, which usually is the gold standard. This method involves the graphical construction of a Bland-Altmann plot which is used to compare the measurements from both methods.

chapters.title: Facets of Clinical Research and Biostatistics

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about simple random sampling?
options: It is the sampling method of choice for heterogenous population
Members are selected without specifying any criteria for selection
Every 5th or 10th member is picked at regular interval
Population is first divided into strata then sampled randomly
questions.explanation: In simple random sampling, samples are drawn in such a way that every element in a population has equal chances of being included. In other words, the members are selected without specifying any criteria for selection.

questions.stem: A study on the prevalence of diabetes was conducted and the sampling method shown below was used. Identify the sampling method used. [[IMG:1]] [[IMG:2]] [[IMG:3]]
questions.explanation: In this study, the population is separated into homogenous sub-groups and from these, random samples are drawn. This sampling method is called stratified random sampling.

questions.stem: 881 Which of the following is incorrect about cluster sampling?
options: Clusters are created based on similarities
It is a two stage sampling
It is cheaper than most other methods
It is a method used for rapid assessment
questions.explanation: In cluster sampling, the clusters are created randomly. On the contrary, in stratified random sampling, the strata or groups are created based on similarities.

questions.stem: Which sampling method is used for assessing the immunization status of children under the immunization program?
questions.explanation: Cluster sampling is the method of sampling done in immunization programs for assessing the immunization status of children.

questions.stem: A research is being conducted to assess the nutritional status of the children in a particular district. For this purpose, 2 children are randomly selected from every school in the district. What is this type of sampling known as?
questions.explanation: In the cluster sampling technique, the sub-groups of the population/ clusters are naturally occurring. These clusters are randomly made rather than based on any particular characteristic. The population of children here is naturally divided into various schools without being based on any characteristics.

questions.stem: In which of the following sampling techniques is design effect used? 882
questions.explanation:
The design effect is used in cluster sampling to allow for design structure and correlation between clusters.
The design effect (DEFF) is used to decide the sample size needed for cluster sampling. This is done by calculating the difference in sampling variability to the variability expected with simple random sampling (SRS).
It can more simply be stated as the actual sample size divided by the effective sample size (what you would expect if you were using SRS). For example, let’s say you were using cluster sampling. A DEFF of 2 means the variance is twice as large as you would expect with SRS. It also means that if you used cluster sampling, you’d have to use twice the sample size.

questions.stem: Simple random sampling is ideal for which of the following study groups?
options: A study being conducted on all vaccinated people of an area
A study on occupational exposure in all workers of the same factory
A study being conducted on prevalence of acute gastroenteritis in all school children of an area
A study on prevalence of hypertension in men aged 50-75 years in an area
questions.explanation:
Simple random sampling is ideal for a homogeneous population as the sample would be completely representative of the population and it would eliminate the need for systematization or stratification. Here, workers of the same factory form a homogeneous population.
Option A: For a vaccinated population - cluster sampling
Options C and D: For a heterogeneous population - stratified sampling

questions.stem: In a study, first schools were sampled, then sections and finally students. What is this type of sampling known as?
questions.explanation:
Multistage sampling is the taking of samples in stages using smaller and smaller sampling units at each stage. It involves dividing the population into groups (or clusters). Then, one or more clusters are chosen at random and everyone within the chosen cluster is sampled.
Snowball sampling is a type of non-random sampling preferred in case of diseases with social stigma (eg., alcoholism, iv drug abuse etc).

questions.stem: For an epidemiological study, sampling was done as shown below. What is this type of sampling known as? [[IMG:1]] [[IMG:2]] [[IMG:3]] 883
questions.explanation: Systematic sampling involves a systematic pattern to sampling, like choosing every 3rd person from an area or hospital, etc.

questions.stem: In a study, subjects were assigned according to the potential factor that will influence the outcome of the study. What is this type of sampling known as?
questions.explanation:
In stratified random sampling, the population is first divided into homogeneous groups or strata. From these strata, random samples are drawn.
For example: If a researcher wants to conduct a research study to determine if alcohol consumption is a risk factor for lung cancer. He must first stratify the population into smokers and non-smokers because smoking is a known risk factor and also smoking is associated with
alcohol consumption.

questions.explanation: The image shown is that of an asymmetric funnel plot. This usually occurs in meta-analysis due to publication bias or other reporting bias.

questions.stem: Results of various studies carried out to study the role of smoking in breast cancer are plotted below. Identify the plot.
questions.explanation: The image shown is that of a forest plot used for plotting the results of a meta-analysis.

questions.stem: A study was done to assess the risk factors for breast cancer in 100 females from urban cities. A statistical group and analysis are shown below. The values indicate the odds ratio and the 95% confidence interval. How many risk factors may be ascertained from the statistical analysis of the research? [[IMG:1]]
questions.explanation:
Among the factors shown in the above statistical group, the odds ratio of early menarche, BRCA mutation, and obesity show positive association and are statistically significant. Hence these 3 factors can be ascertained as risk factors.
High socioeconomic status is not a risk factor. Even though there is a positive association, it is not statistically significant. Any association that has a 95% confidence interval range that includes the value of 1.0 is considered to be non-significant. The value of 1.0 in the range means that the two factors may co-exist together but one is not causing the other to happen.
Odds ratio (OR) is the key parameter in case-control studies to assess the strength of association between the exposure and outcome. The interpretation of the odds ratio can be done as below:
OR > 1 indicates a positive association. If both upper and lower limits of the 95% confidence limits are also >1, it suggests that the odds ratio is significant and the factor can be ascertained as a risk factor.
OR = 1indicates no association. Irrespective of the odds ratio, if the lower limit of 95% CI is <1 and the upper limit of 95% CI >1, the OR is non-significant and cannot be ascertained either as a protective or a risk factor.
OR < 1 indicates a negative association. If both upper and lower limits of the 95% confidence limits are also <1, it suggests that the odds ratio is significant and the factor can be ascertained as a protective factor.
Interpretation of the individual factors given in the question:
Factor | Odds ratio(95%confidence li mits) | Interpretation
Early menarche | 1.3(1.2-1.9) | Positive association, significa nt,risk factor
Age <50 years | 0.04 (0.01-0.32) | Negative association, signific ant, protective factor
Smoking | 0.5 (0.02-0.9) | Negative association, signific ant, protective factor
BRCA mutation | 1.9 (1.1-2.8) | Positive association, significa nt,risk factor
Alcohol | 1.0 (0.8-1.8) | No association, non-significa nt
High socioeconomic status | 1.4 (0.5-3.5) | Positive association, non-sign ificant
Obesity | 1.24 (1.1-1.7) | Positive association, significa nt,risk factor
No family history of Ca. brea st | 0.3 (0.01-0.9) | Negative association, signific ant, protective factor

questions.explanation: The Dixon’s Q test is used for identification and rejection of outliers. It is usually used in normal distributions.

questions.stem: Which of the following is false about mental health?
options: Mental disorders are universal, not specific to any group
Mental health is the mere absence of mental illness
Heredity can contribute to mental illnesses
Substance abuse is a type of mental illness
questions.explanation:
Mental health is a state of well-being in which an individual realizes his or her own abilities and not merely the absence of mental illness. It is the ability to cope with stress, be productive, and contribute to the community.
Mental disorders are universal and are not specific to any particular group. They are associated with hereditary (family history of psychiatric disorders) and environmental factors. Substance abuse and alcohol addiction are considered types of mental illness.

questions.stem: Which of the following are sociopathological factors associated with mental health?
questions.explanation:
Economic insecurity, anxiety, and frustration are the sociopathological factors associated with mental health.
The factors leading to mental health illnesses include:
Organic - cerebral arteriosclerosis, neoplasms, endocrine, metabolic and chronic diseases
Hereditary - schizophrenia
Socio-pathological factors - worries, anxiety, frustration, emotional stress, tension, unhappy marriages, broken homes, poverty, industrialization, urbanization, changing family structure,
population mobility, economic insecurity, cruelty, rejection, neglect.
Environmental - environmental toxins, substance abuse, radiation, nutritional factors, mineral deficiencies, infectious diseases during prenatal, perinatal, and postnatal periods (like rubella), road traffic accidents.

questions.stem: The incidence of mental illness is higher in individuals who are exposed to causal factors during which period of life?
questions.explanation:
Exposure to causal factors during the initial 5 years of life leads to an increased incidence of mental illness.
This period is critical for lifelong mental health behavior and learning, even more crucial than adolescence. During early childhood, the growth and development of children are most
vulnerable to external environmental stressors. A continuous, intimate, and warm relationship with the child's parents during infancy and childhood is very important.

questions.stem: All of the following can be used for the secondary prevention of mental illness in patients except:
questions.explanation:
Improving the social environment is a method of primary prevention of mental illness, not secondary prevention.
The levels of prevention of mental illness and measures are given below:
Primary prevention - improving the social environment and the promotion of mental health awareness
Secondary prevention - early diagnosis and family-based health services like casework and family counseling
Tertiary prevention - measures to reduce the duration of mental illness as well family and community stresses to prevent further breakdown and disruption

questions.stem: Patients with which of the following conditions are considered to have a major mental illness?
questions.explanation:
Patients with manic depressive psychosis are considered to have a major mental illness. Mental health disorders are classified as:
Major (psychotic or not in touch with reality) - include schizophrenia, manic depressive psychosis, and paranoia
Minor (non-psychotic, remain in touch with reality) - include neuroses (like OCD), personality and character disorders
Dementia occurs secondary to organic causes.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a service offered to patients with mental health disorders?
questions.explanation:
Employment services are not included under mental health services. Mental health services include:
Early diagnosis and treatment
Group and individual psychotherapy
Mental health education
Use of modern psychoactive drugs
Rehabilitation
After-care services - help drug-dependent persons to adapt to regular life following treatment and rehabilitation

questions.stem: A 32-year-old man is brought to the casualty with a suspected drug overdose. His sister tells you that he has recently started taking a 'superman drug' after hearing about it from his friends. What drug is she referring to?
questions.explanation:
Amphetamines are also known as the superman drug.
This is because their effects include increased self-confidence and endurance. However, its usage leads to tolerance and dependence.

questions.stem: What is currently the most widely used illicit substance in the world?
questions.explanation:
Cannabis is the most widely used illicit substance in the world.
Cannabis is obtained from Cannabis sativa, C. indica, and C. americana. It is colloquially called marijuana. Other forms of this drug are charas or hashish and bhang.
The image given below shows the cannabis plant.
[[IMG:1]]

questions.stem: What is the most widely used legal addictive substance in India?
questions.explanation: Tobacco is the most widely used legal addictive substance in India, followed closely by alcohol as the second most widely consumed substance.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not an objective of the National Mental Health Programme of 1982?
options: Ensure equal human rights to mentally ill
Promote community participation in mental health services
Promote application of mental health knowledge
Provide accessibility of mental health care
questions.explanation:
Ensuring equal rights to mentally ill people is not an objective of the National Mental Health Programme (NMHP). It was launched in 1982 with the following objectives:
Ensure availability and accessibility of minimum mental health care
Encourage the application of mental health knowledge in general care
Promote community participation in mental health services development
The National Mental Health Programme was relaunched as The Mental Health Care Act, 2017 which includes provisions for equal rights for those with mental illness.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a component of the District Mental Health Programme?
questions.explanation:
Screening is not a component of the District Mental Health Programme. It includes the following components:
Training of all mental health workers at the nodal institute in the state
Increasing public awareness by education to reduce stigma
Early detection and treatment
Providing data for future planning, improvement in service and research Activities by the DMHP for positive mental health include:
School mental health services
College counseling services
Workplace stress management
Suicide prevention services

questions.stem: Which of the following is not included in the Mental Healthcare Act of 2017?
options: Advance directive rights of the mentally ill
Procedure for admission, treatment and discharge of the mentally ill
questions.explanation:
Establishing mobile mental health camps for the benefit of mentally ill patients is not included under the Mental Healthcare Act of 2017.
This act encourages the mobilization of resources to improve mental health care across the country as well as reduce stigma and improve social inclusion/support for those with mental illness. It also has provisions to improve outcomes and protect their rights.
The provisions of this act include:
Rights of persons with mental illness to access health care, live without discrimination and enjoy confidentiality.
Advance directives to allow mentally ill people to make decisions about their treatment
Procedures for admission, treatment (behavioral and interpersonal therapy, medications), and discharge
Decriminalizing suicide and prohibiting electroconvulsive therapy unless anesthesia is used
The act also has clear instructions for the central and state mental health authorities and other mental health establishments on their endeavors.

questions.stem: According to the WHO Mental Health Gap Action Programme, which of the following is not included in the Mental Health Care Act, 2017?
questions.explanation:
According to the WHO Mental Health Gap Action Programme (mhGAP), screening of family members is not included in the Mental Health Care Act, 2017.
The Mental Healthcare Act of 2017 has provisions that include:
Rights of persons with mental illness to access health care, live without discrimination and enjoy confidentiality.
Advance directives to allow mentally ill people to make decisions about their treatment
Procedures for admission, treatment (behavioral and interpersonal therapy, medications), and discharge
Decriminalizing suicide and prohibiting electroconvulsive therapy unless anesthesia is used
These are achieved through the mobilization of resources to required areas, and by providing social support.

questions.stem: The National Suicide Prevention Strategy aims to reduce suicide mortality by in the country by 2030.
questions.explanation:
The National Suicide Prevention Strategy (NSPS) aims to reduce suicide mortality by 10% in India by 2030. It is a multisectoral approach that will involve national and international government ministries, families, communities, and educational institutes to help prevent suicide.
India has a high burden of suicide. It is the leading cause of death among individuals between 15-29 years of age.
Epidemiology
Young and middle-aged adults between 18-45 years
Males more than females
Daily wage earners and people who earn <1,00,000 per annum
Individuals with family issues and illnesses
Hanging and poisoning were the most common methods of suicide. It accounts for >3/4th of all suicides.
Risk factors for suicide
Psychiatric illnesses- Depression, BPD, schizophrenia, and anxiety disorders
Alcohol and other substance abuse disorders
Major physical illness
Job or financial loss
Relationship or social loss
Domestic violence or abuse
Lack of social support
The stigma associated with help-seeking behavior of mental disorders
Lack of social support and sense of isolation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a component of the REDS path in the National suicide prevention strategy?
options: Reduce suicidal deaths by 2% in the next 5 years
Enhance health services to provide suicide prevention strategies
Develop community resilience, and societal support for suicide prevention
questions.explanation:
The National Suicide Prevention Strategy (NSPS) is a multisectoral approach that will involve national and international government ministries, families and communities, and educational institutes. It aims to reduce suicide mortality by 10% in India by 2030.
It recommends REDS path for suicide prevention.
Reinforce leadership, partnership, and institutional capacity in the country
Enhance the health services capacity to provide suicide prevention services
Develop community resilience, societal support for suicide prevention and reduce stigma against suicidal behaviours
Strengthen surveillance and evidence generation. Objectives
To establish effective surveillance mechanism for suicide prevention in next 3 years
To establish psychiatric OPDs that provide suicide prevention services through District Mental Health Programme, within next 5 years
To integrate mental well-being curriculum in all educational institutes within next 8 years.

questions.stem: A 42-year-old male prisoner is being evaluated for aggressive tendencies and antisocial behavior. Which of the following genotypes is associated with these symptoms?
questions.explanation:
XYY genotype is often associated with aggressive tendencies, antisocial, and often, criminal behavior. It is called Jacob’s syndrome.
Option A: XXY genotype is associated with Klinefelter's syndrome. Option B: XO genotype is associated with Turner's syndrome.
Option C: Triple X syndrome is associated with genotype XXX. It is also called super female.

questions.stem: What is the risk of developing Down's syndrome in a baby born to a 45-year-old woman?
questions.explanation:
The risk of developing Down’s syndrome in a baby born to a 45-year-old woman is 1 in 50.
The risk of developing of Down's syndrome in a baby born to a 20-year-old woman is around 1 in 3000 and it increases with rising maternal age. It is an autosomal disorder caused by trisomy of chromosome 21.

questions.stem: Which of the following conditions is not autosomal dominant?
questions.explanation:
Ataxia-telangiectasia or Louis-Bar syndrome is an autosomal recessive condition. Autosomal dominant conditions include:
Neurofibromatosis
Marfan’s syndrome
Retinoblastoma
Huntington's chorea
Polycystic kidney disease

questions.stem: Which of the following is incorrect regarding autosomal recessive disorders?
options: Both male and female offspring are affected
Most inborn errors of metabolism have this form of inheritance
It affects more people at a later age than in childhood
questions.explanation:
Autosomal recessive disorders usually manifest in childhood or earlier.
Heterozygotes are unaffected by the disease. When both parents are heterozygous, each offspring (both male and female) has a 1:4 chance of being affected. Examples of autosomal recessive disorders include several inborn errors of metabolism like phenylketonuria, cystic fibrosis, and galactosemia.

questions.stem: A 6-year-old boy with recurrent hemarthrosis was found to have deficiency of factor VIII. He was adopted and his family history is unknown. What is the inheritance pattern of this condition?
questions.explanation:
The given clinical scenario is suggestive of hemophilia A. It is an X-linked recessive disorder. Hemophilia is of two types:
Hemophilia A - due to mutations in the F8 gene leading to factor VIII deficiency
Hemophilia B - due to mutations in the F9 gene leading to factor IX deficiency
Affected children often present with prolonged bleeding after procedures like circumcision or major bleeds like intracranial hemorrhages. When the child begins to walk, bleeding into the joint (hemarthrosis) may occur, causing painful swellings and reddening.
Laboratory investigations show elevated aPTT, with normal PT and platelet count. It is treated by the administration of factor VIII or factor IX concentrates.

questions.stem: A pathologist is examining the peripheral smear of a patient with anemia. Which of the following is incorrect about the epidemiology of this disease? [[IMG:1]]
options: It is prevalent in areas with high frequency of malaria
It is an autosomal dominant disorder
Couples at risk can undergo prenatal testing and diagnosis
It manifests during the first year of life
questions.explanation:
The given peripheral smear shows sickling of RBCs, suggestive of sickle cell anemia. It is an autosomal recessive disorder.
The prevalence is high among Africans. This disorder usually has its onset during the first year of life. Couples at risk can opt for prenatal testing and diagnosis as well.

questions.stem: What was the primary goal of the Human Genome Project?
options: To introduce a gene sequence into a cell
To develop new diagnostic techniques for genetic disorders
To determine the sequence of nucleotide base pairs in human DNA
To study the precise genetic composition of specific populations
questions.explanation:
The primary goal of the Human Genome Project was to determine the sequence of nucleotide base pairs that make up human DNA and to map all genes from the human genome (20,500 genes).
The project was launched in 1990 and deemed complete in 2003.

questions.stem: What is Hardy-Weinberg law related to?
questions.explanation:
The Hardy-Weinberg law is related to population genetics. Population genetics is the study of the precise genetic composition of a population and various factors determining the incidence of inherited traits in them.
Founder effect is a violation to this law. It is due to difference in expression of the genes in founding population. This is responsible for the difference in the distribution of disease in population.

questions.stem: The Hardy-Weinberg law is applicable in populations with which of the following?
questions.explanation: The Hardy-Weinberg law is applicable for infinitely large, static populations with random mating.

questions.stem: Match the following.
questions.explanation:
Positive eugenics encourages the breeding of those with desirable phenotypes. Negative eugenics discourages the breeding of those with undesirable phenotypes. Euthenics is the environmental manipulation to enable genes to express themselves.
Euphenics is the science of making phenotypic improvements in humans after birth, generally to affect a problematic genetic condition.

questions.stem: A young woman with a family history of beta-thalassemia is planning to marry her first cousin. Which of the following will you recommend for this woman?
questions.explanation:
This young woman must be advised to undergo prospective counseling.
It refers to the process explaining to heterozygous individuals the risk of having affected children if they marry another heterozygous individual. It is performed prior to conception.
Retrospective counseling is performed after the genetic disorder has already occurred in the first child.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old pregnant woman is planned for amniocentesis. What is the gestational age at which it can be done at the earliest?
questions.explanation:
Amniocentesis can be done as early as 14 weeks of gestation.
It refers to the examination of a sample of amniotic fluid to diagnose chromosomal disorders and some metabolic errors. It is indicated in the following cases:
Pregnant women aged 35 years or above
Family history of:
Chromosomal abnormalities
Metabolic errors
Chromosomal translocation
Sex-linked genetic disease

questions.stem: What is a Punnett square used for?
questions.explanation:
A Punnett square is a diagram used to predict the probability of a particular genotype in an offspring.
It is a standard tool for genetic counselors. The image given below shows a Punnett square.
[[IMG:1]]

questions.stem: The risk of genetic diseases in consanguineous marriage between first cousins is?
questions.explanation: The risk of genetic diseases in consanguineous marriage between first cousins is 4-8%. The risk of genetic diseases in non-consanguineous marriage is 2-4%.
